screen.title: Announcement: Fire drill
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement in a residence hall.

audio.text: Good morning, residents of Hall B. A fire drill is scheduled for tomorrow at ten a.m. When the alarm sounds, please leave by the nearest stairway, and do not use the elevators. Gather on the lawn across the street and wait until a staff member tells you it's safe to return. The drill should take about fifteen minutes. Thank you for your cooperation.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the announcement?
options: To report a fire in Hall B
To prepare residents for a safety exercise
To announce repairs to the elevators
To invite residents to an event on the lawn

why.en: Purpose (paraphrase of "fire drill"). A takes "fire" literally; D misuses "lawn".
why.tr: Amaç ("fire drill" parafrazı). A "fire" kelimesini gerçek yangın sanıyor; D "lawn" kelimesini yanlış kullanıyor.
why.es: Propósito (paráfrasis de "fire drill"). A toma "fire" de forma literal; D usa mal "lawn".

questions.stem: What are residents told to do?
options: Take the elevators to the ground floor
Wait outside until staff say they can return
Stay in their rooms for about fifteen minutes
Meet in the lobby of Hall B

why.en: Detail (paraphrase). A contradicts "do not use the elevators"; C misuses "fifteen minutes".
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz). A "asansör kullanmayın" ile çelişiyor; C "on beş dakika" bilgisini yanlış kullanıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis). A contradice "do not use the elevators"; C usa mal "fifteen minutes".

questions.stem: What does the speaker recommend?
options: Registering online for a seat
Bringing a participation form
Sitting in the assigned section
Arriving before the talk begins

why.tr: Ayrıntı ("birkaç dakika erken gelin" parafrazı). C "numaralı oturma yok" bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "arrive a few minutes early"). C contradice "no assigned seating".

screen.title: Announcement: New thesis portal
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement for graduate students.

audio.text: Good afternoon, graduate students. Starting next month, theses will be submitted through the new online portal instead of by email. Printed copies are no longer required, except in the architecture program, where students should still deliver two bound copies to the department office.

questions.stem: What is changing?
options: The formatting rules for theses
The deadline for submitting theses
The way theses are handed in
The number of copies every student prints

why.en: Main change (paraphrase of "submitted through the new online portal instead of by email"). A: the rules are only checked, not changed.
why.tr: Ana değişiklik ("e-posta yerine çevrim içi portal" parafrazı). A: kurallar değişmiyor, yalnızca kontrol ediliyor.
why.es: Cambio principal (paráfrasis de "submitted through the new online portal instead of by email"). A: las normas solo se revisan, no cambian.

questions.stem: What is implied about students who wait until the last day to submit?
options: They will automatically receive a lower grade for being late.
They will have to deliver two bound copies.
They will be allowed to send the thesis by email.
They may not have time to fix formatting problems.

why.en: Inference from "allow extra time for corrections". B applies only to architecture students.
why.tr: Çıkarım: "düzeltmeler için fazladan zaman ayırın". B yalnızca mimarlık öğrencileri için geçerli.
why.es: Inferencia a partir de "allow extra time for corrections". B solo se aplica a los estudiantes de arquitectura.

screen.title: Announcement: Lab safety training
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement in a chemistry class.

audio.text: Before next week's first lab, everyone must complete our two-part safety training. Part one is an online module, which takes about forty minutes and ends with a short quiz. Part two is a hands-on session in the lab. Your access card will open the lab door only once both parts are recorded, and records can take up to two days to update, so please don't leave the quiz until the night before.

questions.stem: What is the announcement mainly about?
options: Steps students must complete before using the lab
A change to the date of the first lab session
Problems that students have had with access cards
How the safety quiz will count toward the final grade

why.en: Main topic: the two-part training required before lab access. C misuses "access card", which is only how the rule is enforced; D invents a grading rule.
why.tr: Ana konu: laboratuvara girmeden önce gereken iki aşamalı eğitim. C kuralın uygulanma biçimi olan "access card" ifadesini yanlış kullanıyor; D olmayan bir notlandırma kuralı uyduruyor.
why.es: Tema principal: la formación en dos partes necesaria antes de entrar al laboratorio. C usa mal "access card", que solo es cómo se aplica la norma; D se inventa una regla de calificación.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker tell students not to wait until the night before?
options: The online module closes on the weekend
The quiz is harder than it looks
Their card might not open the door in time
Hands-on sessions fill up quickly

why.en: Inference: records "can take up to two days to update", so a last-minute quiz could leave a student locked out of the first lab. D gives a reason the speaker never mentions.
why.tr: Çıkarım: kayıtlar "can take up to two days to update", yani son gece çözülen sınav öğrenciyi ilk laboratuvarda kapıda bırakabilir. D konuşmacının hiç söylemediği bir gerekçe.
why.es: Inferencia: los registros "can take up to two days to update", así que hacer la prueba la víspera podría dejar al estudiante sin acceso al primer laboratorio. D da un motivo que el hablante nunca menciona.

options: Attendance is required in order to apply
Students will receive course credit for attending
The session will not be offered again this year
Spaces at some universities are taken quickly

why.es: Motivo (paráfrasis de "places ... usually fill within two weeks"). B usa mal "course credit", que solo es uno de los temas; A y C nunca se dicen.

screen.title: Announcement: Final exam rooms
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement in a psychology class.

options: The usual room cannot hold the whole class
Baker Hall will be closed on Thursday
The professor wants students to sit farther apart
The start time of the exam has been moved

why.en: Inference: "so many of you are registered" implies that the usual room is too small. D contradicts "The start time hasn't changed"; B is wrong because the auditorium is in Baker Hall.
why.tr: Çıkarım: "so many of you are registered" ifadesi her zamanki sınıfın küçük kaldığını gösteriyor. D "The start time hasn't changed" ile çelişiyor; B yanlış, çünkü amfi de Baker Hall'da.
why.es: Inferencia: "so many of you are registered" implica que el aula de siempre es demasiado pequeña. D contradice "The start time hasn't changed"; B es incorrecta porque el auditorio está en Baker Hall.

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about students whose last names begin with M to Z?
options: They will take the exam on a different day
They should go to the Baker Hall auditorium
They may need to leave earlier than usual
They will be given extra time on the exam

why.tr: Çıkarım: Morris binası on dakikalık yürüme mesafesinde ve başlama saati aynı; bu yüzden bu öğrenciler daha erken yola çıkmalı. B A–L harfleriyle başlayanların salonu; D hiç söylenmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: el edificio Morris está a diez minutos a pie y la hora de inicio es la misma, así que estos estudiantes deberían salir antes. B es el aula de los apellidos de la A a la L; D no se menciona.

screen.title: Announcement: Orientation schedule change
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement at an orientation event.

audio.text: Good morning, and welcome to all our new international students. There's one change to today's schedule. Because of the rain, the campus tour planned for eleven will now start at one-thirty, and lunch, which was planned for one-thirty, will be served at eleven instead, in the main hall. questions.stem: What change does the speaker announce?
options: Lunch has been canceled because of the weather
The tour will now take place inside the main hall
The orientation will end earlier than planned
Two of the day's activities have switched times

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): the tour moved from eleven to one-thirty and lunch moved to eleven, so the two events swapped. B reuses "main hall", which is where lunch will be served; A is wrong because lunch is only moved, not canceled.
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): tur saat on birden bir buçuğa, öğle yemeği de on bire alındı; yani iki etkinliğin saatleri yer değiştirdi. B "main hall" ifadesini kullanıyor ama orası yemeğin verileceği yer; A yanlış, çünkü yemek iptal edilmedi, sadece saati değişti.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): la visita pasó de las once a la una y media y el almuerzo pasó a las once, así que los dos eventos intercambiaron sus horas. B reutiliza "main hall", que es donde se servirá el almuerzo; A es incorrecta porque el almuerzo solo cambia de hora, no se cancela.

questions.stem: Why should students pick up a welcome packet?
options: It has a card they need to get into the library
It shows the new route of the campus tour
It includes a ticket for lunch in the main hall
It explains how to apply for a permanent ID

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): the packet contains a temporary student card "which you'll need to enter the library". C mixes in lunch, which is mentioned earlier; D twists "temporary".
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): pakette "which you'll need to enter the library" denen geçici öğrenci kartı var. C daha önce geçen öğle yemeğini karıştırıyor; D "temporary" kelimesini çarpıtıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): el paquete contiene una tarjeta temporal de estudiante "which you'll need to enter the library". C mezcla el almuerzo, que se menciona antes; D tergiversa "temporary".

screen.title: Announcement: Quiet hours before exams
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement in a residence hall.

options: Final exams will start on Monday
The study room will close at ten

questions.stem: What is true about the study room?
options: It will be open all night
It is on the second floor
It closes at eight p.m.

screen.title: Announcement: Wi-Fi maintenance
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement made to students.

audio.text: Attention, students. Campus Wi-Fi will be unavailable this Sunday from midnight until six a.m. while the IT department installs new equipment. questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To ask students to report problems with the Wi-Fi
To warn students about a planned break in wireless service
To announce new opening hours for the library lab
To explain how to create a new network password

why.en: Purpose (paraphrase): the Wi-Fi will be off early on Sunday for maintenance. C turns the detail about the library lab into the purpose; D goes beyond "sign in to the network again", since no new password is mentioned.
why.tr: Amaç (parafraz): bakım nedeniyle pazar sabahı erken saatlerde Wi-Fi olmayacak. C kütüphane laboratuvarıyla ilgili ayrıntıyı ana amaç yapıyor; D "sign in to the network again" ifadesinin ötesine geçiyor, çünkü yeni bir şifreden söz edilmiyor.
why.es: Propósito (paráfrasis): el wifi no funcionará el domingo de madrugada por mantenimiento. C convierte el detalle del laboratorio de la biblioteca en el propósito; D va más allá de "sign in to the network again", porque no se menciona ninguna contraseña nueva.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention the library's basement lab?
options: It is where the new equipment will be installed
Students should collect their passwords there
Its computers will still have internet access
It will be closed on Sunday morning for the work

why.en: Function: the lab's computers use cables, so they "keep working" during the outage. D says the opposite; A confuses the lab with the place where the IT work happens.
why.tr: İşlev: laboratuvardaki bilgisayarlar kabloyla bağlı, bu yüzden kesinti sırasında "keep working". D bunun tersini söylüyor; A laboratuvarı bilgi işlem çalışmasının yapılacağı yerle karıştırıyor.
why.es: Función: los ordenadores del laboratorio usan cable, así que "keep working" durante el corte. D dice lo contrario; A confunde el laboratorio con el lugar donde se hará el trabajo técnico.

A monthly online meeting that is open to every third-year student in the school

screen.title: Announcement: Elevator repairs
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement made to students.

An elevator that will not work for a few days

screen.title: Announcement: Flu vaccination day
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement made to students.

audio.text: Good morning, everyone. The student health center is holding a free flu vaccination day this Wednesday from nine to four. It will take place in the gym, not at the health center, because the center is being painted this week. No appointment is needed, but please bring your student ID. If you can't come on Wednesday, you can book a shot at the health center starting next week.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To tell students about a free flu shot event
To explain why the health center will close for good
To remind students to renew their student IDs
To invite students to help paint the health center

why.en: Main purpose (paraphrase). B overstates the painting into a permanent closure; C and D misuse details (the ID, the painting).
why.tr: Ana amaç (parafraz). B boyamayı kalıcı kapanmaya dönüştürüyor; C ve D ayrıntıları yanlış kullanıyor (kimlik kartı, boya).
why.es: Propósito principal (paráfrasis). B convierte la pintura en un cierre definitivo; C y D usan mal los detalles (el carné, la pintura).

questions.stem: Why will the event be held in the gym?
options: The gym is closer to most dormitories
The health center building is being painted
Too many students are expected for the center
The gym is open for longer hours

why.en: Detail (paraphrase of "because the center is being painted this week"). C sounds reasonable but is not the reason given; A and D are never mentioned.
why.tr: Ayrıntı ("because the center is being painted this week" ifadesinin parafrazı). C mantıklı görünüyor ama söylenen neden bu değil; A ve D hiç geçmiyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "because the center is being painted this week"). C parece razonable, pero no es el motivo que se da; A y D no se mencionan.

screen.title: Announcement: A lottery for concert tickets
screen.prompt: Listen to an announcement made to students.

audio.text: Good afternoon. Because tickets for the spring concert sold out within minutes last year, we're trying something different. Instead of selling tickets first come, first served, we'll hold a lottery. Enter online by Friday. Winners will be emailed on Monday and must pay within forty-eight hours, or their tickets will go to the next name on the list. Each student may enter only once.

questions.stem: Why is the lottery being introduced?
options: The concert hall has fewer seats this year
The website could not handle online payments
Students complained that tickets were too expensive
Tickets were gone too quickly under the old system

why.en: Reason (paraphrase of "sold out within minutes last year"). A, B and C give reasons the speaker never mentions.
why.tr: Neden ("sold out within minutes last year" ifadesinin parafrazı). A, B ve C konuşmacının hiç söylemediği nedenler veriyor.
why.es: Motivo (paráfrasis de "sold out within minutes last year"). A, B y C dan razones que la hablante nunca menciona.

questions.stem: What will happen if a winner has not paid by Wednesday evening, more than two days after the email?
options: The winner will be charged a late fee
The winner will be entered in next year's lottery
Another student will be offered the ticket
The ticket will be sold at the door instead

why.en: Inference: winners are emailed on Monday and have forty-eight hours, so by Wednesday evening the time is up and the ticket "will go to the next name on the list". A, B and D are not stated.
why.tr: Çıkarım: kazananlara Pazartesi e-posta gidiyor ve kırk sekiz saatleri var; Çarşamba akşamı süre dolmuş olur ve bilet "listedeki bir sonraki isme" geçer. A, B ve D söylenmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: a los ganadores se les escribe el lunes y tienen cuarenta y ocho horas, así que el miércoles por la tarde el plazo ha terminado y la entrada "pasa al siguiente nombre de la lista". A, B y D no se dicen.

why.es: Respuesta indirecta: la venta se aplazó, y este es el motivo. A repite "on sale" y "noon"; B dice "Yes" sobre otro plan; C da un dato que no viene al caso.

audio.text: I'll believe the bike share is cheaper when I see it.

options: I saw a red bike outside the library.
Sharing a room is usually much cheaper than living alone.

Do the math: the free thirty minutes cover most trips.

why.en: Skeptical idiom ("I'll believe it when I see it") → an argument against the doubt. A repeats "see" literally; C repeats "believe"; B repeats "share" and "cheaper" about housing.
why.tr: Şüpheci deyim ("I'll believe it when I see it") → şüpheye karşı bir argüman. A "see" kelimesini gerçek anlamıyla tekrar ediyor; C "believe" kelimesini tekrar ediyor; B "share" ve "cheaper" kelimelerini barınma için tekrar ediyor.
why.es: Expresión escéptica ("I'll believe it when I see it") → un argumento contra la duda. A repite "see" en sentido literal; C repite "believe"; B repite "share" y "cheaper" sobre la vivienda.

audio.text: Something tells me the interview went better than you expected.

options: Something is wrong with my phone again.
I expected the bus to be late again, and of course it was.

The interview room was on the third floor.

why.en: Indirect "yes": being asked about a start date means the interview went very well. A repeats "something"; B repeats "expected"; D repeats "interview" but only gives a place.
why.tr: Dolaylı "evet": başlama tarihinin sorulması görüşmenin çok iyi geçtiğini gösteriyor. A "something" kelimesini tekrar ediyor; B "expected" kelimesini tekrar ediyor; D "interview" kelimesini tekrar ediyor ama yalnızca yer söylüyor.
why.es: Un "sí" indirecto: que le pregunten cuándo puede empezar significa que la entrevista fue muy bien. A repite "something"; B repite "expected"; D repite "interview" pero solo da un lugar.

audio.text: Is it just me, or is the study room app impossible to use?

options: Just me and two friends from my class.
The study rooms are all on the second floor of the library.
I use my phone mostly for music.

why.en: "Is it just me" asks for agreement → a partial agreement with encouragement. A takes "just me" literally; B gives a place; C repeats "use" without answering.
why.tr: "Is it just me" onay istiyor → kısmen katılan ve cesaret veren bir cevap. A "just me" ifadesini gerçek anlamıyla alıyor; B yer söylüyor; C "use" kelimesini cevap vermeden tekrar ediyor.
why.es: "Is it just me" busca acuerdo → un acuerdo parcial con ánimo. A toma "just me" en sentido literal; B da un lugar; C repite "use" sin responder.

Report a problem in her friend's room
Exchange rooms with a student in another hall

why.en: Main topic (paraphrase of "switch dorm rooms"). B adds a reason that is never mentioned; A goes much further than a swap between two students.
why.tr: Ana konu ("switch dorm rooms" ifadesinin parafrazı). B hiç söylenmeyen bir gerekçe ekliyor; A iki öğrenci arasındaki oda değişiminin çok ötesine geçiyor.
why.es: Tema principal (paráfrasis de "switch dorm rooms"). B añade un motivo que nunca se menciona; A va mucho más allá de un intercambio entre dos estudiantes.

questions.stem: What will the woman's friend most likely do next?
options: Submit her own swap request
Inspect the two rooms with the staff
Move into Lin Hall this weekend
Email the office to ask for a date

why.en: Inference: both students must send a swap request, so the friend will come in to fill out hers. C contradicts "Not that fast"; B is the office's job, not the friend's.
why.tr: Çıkarım: iki öğrencinin de değişim talebi göndermesi gerekiyor, bu yüzden arkadaşı kendi formunu doldurmaya gelecek. C "Not that fast" ile çelişiyor; B arkadaşın değil ofisin işi.
why.es: Inferencia: los dos estudiantes deben enviar una solicitud, así que la amiga irá a rellenar la suya. C contradice "Not that fast"; B es tarea de la oficina, no de la amiga.

screen.title: Conversation: A late recommendation letter
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and a financial aid adviser.

audio.text: Hi, the Morgan Scholarship is due on Friday, but one of my professors can't send her recommendation until next week. Will my application still count?
The Friday deadline applies to your part: the essay and the form. Letters are accepted for five working days after that, as long as the recommender sends them to us directly.
Oh, that's a relief. So I shouldn't hold my application until her letter is ready?
Definitely not. If your part arrives late, the committee won't look at it at all.
Got it. I'll finish the essay tonight, then.

questions.stem: Why does the student go to see the adviser?
options: He wants permission to change the topic of his scholarship essay
He needs a form for a different scholarship
He is worried that a late letter will affect his application
He missed the deadline for the scholarship last Friday

why.en: Purpose of the visit: his professor's letter will arrive after the deadline. D misreads the timing (the deadline is this coming Friday); A is never mentioned.
why.tr: Ziyaretin amacı: hocasının mektubu son tarihten sonra gelecek. D zamanlamayı yanlış okuyor (son tarih önümüzdeki cuma); A hiç söz edilmiyor.
why.es: Motivo de la visita: la carta de su profesora llegará después del plazo. D malinterpreta el momento (el plazo es este viernes que viene); A nunca se menciona.

questions.stem: What does the adviser say about the letter?
options: The student's own materials must not be late
Professors should give their letters to the student
The committee may extend the deadline for him
The essay matters less than the application form

why.en: Detail (stated outright): "If your part arrives late, the committee won't look at it". B contradicts "sends them to us directly"; C is the opposite of what she says.
why.tr: "If your part arrives late, the committee won't look at it" ifadesinde açıkça söyleniyor (ayrıntı). B "sends them to us directly" bilgisiyle çelişiyor; C söylediğinin tam tersi.
why.es: Detalle (dicho de forma directa): "If your part arrives late, the committee won't look at it". B contradice "sends them to us directly"; C es lo contrario de lo que dice.

screen.title: Conversation: Booking a tutor
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and a receptionist at the peer tutoring center.

audio.text: Hi, I'd like to see a tutor for my economics course. Is anyone free this afternoon?
Let me check. Our economics tutors are fully booked today, but there's an opening tomorrow at eleven.
I've got a lab then. Is there anything later in the day?
Not tomorrow, no. But we also run a drop-in group session on Thursday evenings. You don't need an appointment, just bring your questions.
That might actually suit me better. Most of my questions are about the chapter everyone's stuck on.

questions.stem: Why can't the student meet a tutor tomorrow at eleven?
options: The tutor will be leading a group
He has another class at that time
The center is closed in the morning
No economics tutors work that day

why.en: Detail (paraphrase of "I've got a lab then"). C and D contradict the eleven o'clock opening; A confuses the tutor with the Thursday group session.
why.tr: Ayrıntı ("I've got a lab then" ifadesinin parafrazı). C ve D saat on birdeki boş randevuyla çelişiyor; A tutor'ı perşembe akşamki grup oturumuyla karıştırıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "I've got a lab then"). C y D contradicen el hueco de las once; A confunde al tutor con la sesión de grupo del jueves.

questions.stem: What will the student probably do?
options: Return to the center this afternoon
Ask his lab instructor for help
Attend a group session without booking
Reserve a private tutor for next week

why.en: Inference: he says the drop-in session "might actually suit me better". A is impossible because today's tutors are fully booked; B is never mentioned.
why.tr: Çıkarım: randevusuz grup oturumu için "might actually suit me better" diyor. A imkânsız, çünkü bugünkü tutorların hepsi dolu; B hiç söz edilmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: dice que la sesión sin cita "might actually suit me better". A es imposible porque hoy los tutores están completos; B nunca se menciona.

screen.title: Conversation: Selling textbooks back
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and a bookstore clerk.

audio.text: Hi, I'd like to sell back these two textbooks from last semester.
Sure. I can give you twenty-two dollars for the biology one. But there's a new edition of the economics book coming out, so we can't buy that one back.
Oh no. Is there anything I can do with it?
You could post it on the student exchange page. The summer economics course is still using the old edition.
Good idea. I'll put it up tonight.

questions.stem: What is the man's problem?
options: He has lost the receipt for his textbooks.
He paid too much for his biology book.
The store will not take one of his books.
He needs the new edition of a textbook.

why.en: Problem (paraphrase): the store "can't buy that one back" because a new edition is coming out. D is the trap: the new edition is the reason, but the man does not need it. A is never mentioned.
why.tr: Sorun (parafraz): yeni baskı çıkacağı için mağaza "can't buy that one back". D tuzak: yeni baskı sebebin kendisi ama adamın ona ihtiyacı yok. A hiç geçmiyor.
why.es: Problema (paráfrasis): la tienda "can't buy that one back" porque va a salir una nueva edición. D es la trampa: la nueva edición es el motivo, pero el chico no la necesita. A no se menciona.

questions.stem: Why does the woman mention the summer economics course?
options: To suggest that some students may still want his book
To recommend that he take the course next summer
To explain why the new edition costs more
To tell him when the store will buy books again

why.en: Function: the summer course still uses the old edition, so students in it may buy his copy. B misreads the course as advice for the man; D is not mentioned; C is not discussed at all.
why.tr: İşlev: yaz dersi hâlâ eski baskıyı kullanıyor, yani o dersteki öğrenciler onun kitabını alabilir. B dersi adama verilmiş bir tavsiye sanıyor; D konuşmada geçmiyor; C hiç tartışılmıyor.
why.es: Función: el curso de verano sigue usando la edición antigua, así que sus estudiantes podrían comprarle el libro. B interpreta el curso como un consejo para él; D no se menciona; C no se trata en absoluto.

screen.title: Conversation: Credit for an internship
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and an academic advisor.

audio.text: Hi, I've got a summer internship at an architecture firm, and I'd like course credit for it. I've filled in the form.
Good. Has your supervisor at the firm signed it?
Not yet. She's away until next week, and the form's due Friday.

Technically, that's a problem. But if you hand it in now with a note saying when she'll sign, the department usually accepts that. What matters more is a faculty sponsor. Without one, there's no credit at all.
Oh. Then I'd better email Professor Lund today.

questions.stem: What is the woman worried about?
options: Her internship might not be at an approved firm
Her supervisor has refused to sign the form
Her form may be incomplete when it is due
She will not have time to email her professor

why.en: Concern (paraphrase): her supervisor is away until next week, but the form is due Friday. B is too strong: the supervisor has not refused, she is simply away. A is never mentioned.
why.tr: Endişe (parafraz): amiri gelecek haftaya kadar yok ama form cuma günü teslim edilmeli. B fazla iddialı: amir imzalamayı reddetmedi, sadece şu anda burada değil. A konuşmada hiç geçmiyor.
why.es: Preocupación (paráfrasis): su supervisora no vuelve hasta la semana que viene, pero el formulario se entrega el viernes. B es demasiado fuerte: la supervisora no se ha negado, simplemente está fuera. A no se menciona.

questions.stem: What does the man imply?
options: The deadline for the form will probably be extended for her
Finding a faculty sponsor is her most important task
The supervisor's signature is not needed at all
Professor Lund rarely agrees to sponsor interns

why.en: Inference: the missing signature can be handled with a note, but "what matters more" is a sponsor, and without one there is no credit. C goes too far, because the signature is still needed, only later; A is never suggested.
why.tr: Çıkarım: eksik imza bir notla çözülebilir ama "what matters more" bir öğretim üyesi danışman bulmak; o olmadan kredi yok. C fazla ileri gidiyor, çünkü imza yine gerekli, sadece daha sonra; A hiç önerilmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: la firma que falta se puede resolver con una nota, pero "what matters more" es tener un profesor patrocinador, y sin él no hay créditos. C va demasiado lejos, porque la firma sigue siendo necesaria, solo que más tarde; A no se sugiere en ningún momento.

screen.title: Conversation: Joining a volleyball league
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and an employee at the recreation center.

audio.text: Hi, I'd like to join the intramural volleyball league, but I'm not on a team.
That's fine. You can sign up as a free agent, and we'll place you on a team that needs players.
Great. Is there a fee?
It's ten dollars a player, but each team pays as a group, so once you're placed, you'll pay your captain.
And when do games start?
The week after next, on Tuesday or Wednesday evenings.

questions.stem: What will happen after the man signs up?
options: He will be added to a team that is short of players
He will be asked to choose a team captain
He will have to find other players for a new team
He will play his first game on Tuesday this week

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): as a free agent he will be placed "on a team that needs players". C is the opposite; he does not need to form a team. D ignores "the week after next".
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): serbest oyuncu olarak "on a team that needs players" yerleştirilecek. C tam tersi; takım kurması gerekmiyor. D "the week after next" bilgisini yok sayıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): como agente libre lo pondrán "on a team that needs players". C es lo contrario; no tiene que formar un equipo. D ignora "the week after next".

questions.stem: How will the man pay the fee?
options: Online, before he is placed on a team
At the front desk of the recreation center
By paying ten dollars at his first game
By giving the money to his team captain

why.en: Detail: "each team pays as a group … you'll pay your captain". C has the correct amount but the wrong way of paying; B is a usual place to pay, but it is not what she says.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: "each team pays as a group … you'll pay your captain". C doğru tutarı veriyor ama ödeme şekli yanlış; B ödeme için olağan bir yer ama kadının söylediği bu değil.
why.es: Detalle: "each team pays as a group … you'll pay your captain". C da la cantidad correcta, pero la forma de pago es incorrecta; B es un lugar habitual para pagar, pero no es lo que ella dice.

screen.title: Conversation: Borrowing a laptop
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and a library worker.

audio.text: Hi, my laptop is being repaired. Can I borrow one here?
Sure. You can borrow a laptop for up to three days. I just need your student ID.
Here you go. Can I take it home?
Yes, you can. But please bring it back by Friday at five, or you'll have to pay a late fee.
No problem. Thanks!

questions.stem: Why does the woman want to borrow a laptop?
options: She wants to take a test online
Her own laptop is being fixed
She lost her laptop on Friday
The library computers are full

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): "my laptop is being repaired". C misuses "Friday", which is the return day; A and D are not mentioned.
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): "my laptop is being repaired". C iade günü olan "Friday" kelimesini yanlış kullanıyor; A ve D konuşmada geçmiyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): "my laptop is being repaired". C usa mal "Friday", que es el día de devolución; A y D no se mencionan.

questions.stem: What does the man say about the laptop?
options: It must stay in the library
It can be borrowed for a week
It costs five dollars a day
It must be returned by Friday

why.en: Detail: "bring it back by Friday at five". A contradicts "Yes, you can", his answer about taking it home; C misuses "five", which is a time, not a price; B is wrong because the limit is three days.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: "bring it back by Friday at five". A, eve götürme sorusuna verdiği "Yes, you can" cevabıyla çelişiyor; C bir saat olan "five" kelimesini fiyat gibi kullanıyor; B yanlış, çünkü süre üç gün.
why.es: Detalle: "bring it back by Friday at five". A contradice "Yes, you can", su respuesta sobre llevárselo a casa; C usa mal "five", que es una hora y no un precio; B es incorrecta porque el límite es de tres días.

screen.title: Conversation: Asking for a makeup exam
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and a professor.

audio.text: Professor Adeyemi, I'll have to miss next Tuesday's midterm. I'm competing in the regional debate tournament.
Hmm. Makeup exams are really meant for emergencies, and a tournament is planned well in advance.
I know. That's why I'm telling you now instead of afterward.
Fair point. If your debate coach sends me a note, you can take it on Monday afternoon instead. It'll be a different version, though.
That's fine. I'll ask her today.

questions.stem: Why does the man go to see the professor?
options: To ask her to coach the debate team
To find out what the midterm will cover
To complain about the date of the midterm
To arrange another time to take a test

why.en: Purpose (paraphrase): he will miss the midterm and needs to take it at another time. A misuses "coach"; C is wrong because he does not object to the date itself.
why.tr: Amaç (parafraz): ara sınavı kaçıracak ve sınava başka bir zamanda girmesi gerekiyor. A "coach" kelimesini yanlış kullanıyor; C yanlış, çünkü tarihin kendisine itiraz etmiyor.
why.es: Propósito (paráfrasis): va a perderse el examen parcial y necesita hacerlo en otro momento. A usa mal "coach"; C es incorrecta porque no se queja de la fecha en sí.

questions.stem: Why does the man say, "That's why I'm telling you now instead of afterward"?
options: To show that he is giving notice responsibly
To admit that he forgot about an earlier exam
To suggest that the tournament is an emergency
To ask the professor to decide after the event

why.en: Function: he answers her objection by pointing out that he is asking in advance, not after missing the exam. C is the opposite, since he accepts it is not an emergency; D reverses "now instead of afterward".
why.tr: İşlev: hocanın itirazına, sınavı kaçırdıktan sonra değil önceden haber verdiğini vurgulayarak cevap veriyor. C tam tersi, çünkü bunun acil bir durum olmadığını kabul ediyor; D "now instead of afterward" ifadesini tersine çeviriyor.
why.es: Función: responde a la objeción de la profesora señalando que avisa con antelación, no después de perder el examen. C es lo contrario, porque él acepta que no es una emergencia; D invierte "now instead of afterward".

screen.title: Conversation: Booking a writing tutor
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and a receptionist at the writing center.

audio.text: Hi, I'd like to book a session with a writing tutor. My history essay is due on Monday.
Let me see. I'm afraid all the appointments this week are taken. But we have drop-in hours on Thursday from two to five.
Drop-in? So I just come and wait?
Right. Tutors see students in the order they arrive, and it gets busy. Oh, and bring a printed copy of your draft.
Okay. My last class ends at one forty-five, so I'll come straight here.

questions.stem: Why does the woman go to the writing center?
options: To apply for a job as a writing tutor
To ask for more time on her history essay
To pick up a printed copy of her draft
To get help with a paper before it is due

why.en: Purpose (paraphrase): she wants a tutor session before her essay is due on Monday. B is tempting, but she never asks for an extension; C reverses the advice to bring a printed draft.
why.tr: Amaç (parafraz): pazartesi teslim edilecek ödevinden önce bir eğitmenle çalışmak istiyor. B çekici ama ek süre istemiyor; C, basılı taslağı getirme tavsiyesini tersine çeviriyor.
why.es: Propósito (paráfrasis): quiere una sesión con un tutor antes de entregar su ensayo el lunes. B resulta tentadora, pero ella nunca pide una prórroga; C invierte el consejo de traer el borrador impreso.

questions.stem: What does the man imply about the drop-in hours?
options: They are only for students with history essays
Students who arrive late may have a long wait
They have been moved from Thursday to Monday
Students must book them a week in advance

why.en: Inference: tutors see students "in the order they arrive, and it gets busy", so coming late means waiting longer. D contradicts the idea of drop-in hours; C confuses the essay deadline with the drop-in day.
why.tr: Çıkarım: eğitmenler öğrencileri "in the order they arrive, and it gets busy" şeklinde görüyor; yani geç gelen daha uzun bekler. D randevusuz saatler fikriyle çelişiyor; C ödevin teslim gününü randevusuz çalışma günüyle karıştırıyor.
why.es: Inferencia: los tutores atienden "in the order they arrive, and it gets busy", así que quien llega tarde espera más. D contradice la idea de un horario sin cita; C confunde la fecha de entrega con el día de atención sin cita.

screen.title: Conversation: Inviting a guest speaker
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and an employee in the student activities office.

audio.text: Our film club wants to invite a director to speak next month. Is there any funding for that?
There is. Fill out the speaker request on the activities website. We can cover travel, but not a speaking fee.
She lives three hours away, so travel is the main cost anyway.
Then you're in good shape. Just submit it at least three weeks before the event.

questions.stem: What does the woman want to find out?
options: How to start a new film club on campus
Whether the school will pay for a visitor's costs
Which films the director will show next month
How far the director lives from the campus

why.en: Purpose (paraphrase of "Is there any funding for that?"). D is something she tells him, not something she asks; A and C are not discussed.
why.tr: Amaç ("Is there any funding for that?" ifadesinin parafrazı). D onun sorduğu değil, söylediği bir şey; A ve C konuşulmuyor.
why.es: Propósito (paráfrasis de "Is there any funding for that?"). D es algo que ella dice, no algo que pregunta; A y C no se tratan.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the director's visit?
options: The office's rules on payments should not cause a problem
The club will have to pay the director a speaking fee itself
The visit must be moved to a later month
The director has asked the club to pay for a hotel

why.en: Inference: the office pays only for travel, and travel is "the main cost anyway", so "you're in good shape". B ignores that no fee is mentioned; C and D are not stated.
why.tr: Çıkarım: ofis yalnızca yol masrafını ödüyor ve zaten "asıl masraf yol"; bu yüzden "you're in good shape". B hiçbir ücretten söz edilmediğini görmüyor; C ve D söylenmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: la oficina solo paga el viaje, y el viaje es "el gasto principal de todos modos", así que "you're in good shape". B pasa por alto que no se menciona ningún honorario; C y D no se dicen.

screen.title: Conversation: Lab report format
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and a teaching assistant.

audio.text: Excuse me, does the lab report need a title page?
No. Just put your name and the date at the top of the first page.
OK. And how long should it be?
Four pages at most. And don't forget to include your data table at the end.
Great, thanks. I'll add the table tonight.

questions.stem: What does the student ask about first?
options: Where to hand in the report
Whether the report needs a separate title page
When the report is due
Which data to put in the table

why.en: Detail: his first question is "does the lab report need a title page?" A and C are never asked; D confuses the table, which the woman mentions later.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: ilk sorusu "does the lab report need a title page?". A ve C hiç sorulmuyor; D kadının sonra söylediği tabloyu karıştırıyor.
why.es: Detalle: su primera pregunta es "does the lab report need a title page?". A y C no se preguntan; D confunde la tabla, que ella menciona después.

questions.stem: What does the woman remind the student to do?
options: Write at least four pages
Put the date on every page
Include a table of his data
Bring the report to her office

why.tr: Ayrıntı ("don't forget to include your data table" ifadesinin parafrazı). A "four pages at most" ifadesini tersine çeviriyor; B "ilk sayfanın üstü"nü her sayfaya çeviriyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "don't forget to include your data table"). A invierte "four pages at most"; B cambia "la parte superior de la primera página" por todas las páginas.

screen.title: Conversation: An on-campus job interview
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and the manager of the campus museum.

audio.text: Thanks for coming in. The front-desk job here is mostly weekends. Is that a problem?
Saturdays are fine, but I have a lab on Sunday mornings until noon.
Hmm. We open at ten on Sundays. Could you do afternoons only?
Definitely, from one o'clock on.
Good. Most of our weekend visitors come after lunch anyway, so that might actually suit us better.

questions.stem: What problem comes up during the interview?
options: The student cannot work on Saturdays
The museum is closed on Sunday mornings
The student's class schedule overlaps with part of the job
The manager needs someone only on weekdays during the busy season

why.en: Problem (paraphrase): her Sunday lab runs until noon, but the museum opens at ten. A contradicts "Saturdays are fine"; B contradicts "We open at ten on Sundays"; D contradicts "mostly weekends".
why.tr: Sorun (parafraz): Pazar laboratuvarı öğlene kadar sürüyor, müze ise onda açılıyor. A "Saturdays are fine" ile, B "We open at ten on Sundays" ile, D "mostly weekends" ile çelişiyor.
why.es: Problema (paráfrasis): su laboratorio del domingo dura hasta el mediodía, pero el museo abre a las diez. A contradice "Saturdays are fine"; B contradice "We open at ten on Sundays"; D contradice "mostly weekends".

questions.stem: What does the manager imply at the end of the conversation?
options: The student will need to change her lab to another day
The student's limited Sunday hours may not be a disadvantage
The museum will start opening later on Sundays
He will have to find a second person to cover Sunday mornings

why.en: Inference: since most visitors "come after lunch anyway", afternoons "might actually suit us better". D may be true but is not what he implies; A and C are never suggested.
why.tr: Çıkarım: ziyaretçilerin çoğu "zaten öğleden sonra" geldiği için öğleden sonraları "işimize daha iyi gelebilir". D doğru olabilir ama onun ima ettiği bu değil; A ve C hiç önerilmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: como la mayoría de visitantes "viene después de comer de todos modos", las tardes "podrían venirnos mejor". D podría ser cierto pero no es lo que él da a entender; A y C no se proponen.

screen.title: Conversation: A registration mix-up
screen.prompt: Listen to a conversation between a student and an employee at the registrar's office.

audio.text: Hi, I registered for Introduction to Biology last week, but it isn't on my schedule anymore.

questions.stem: Why does the student go to the office?
options: She wants to change the time of her biology lecture
A course she signed up for has disappeared from her schedule
She was charged twice for the same biology course
Her lab partner asked her to switch to a different lab section with him

why.es: Problema principal (paráfrasis de "it isn't on my schedule anymore"). A invierte la petición: quiere recuperar el curso, no cambiar la hora. C y D no se mencionan.

Cancel the student's registration for the course
Ask the biology department to open a new lab
Tell the student to register again next term

why.tr: Çıkarım: onu Perşembe laboratuvarına almayı öneriyor ve öğrenci kabul ediyor ("Please do that"). B ve D "You can" ifadesiyle çelişiyor; C hiç önerilmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: le ofrece pasarla al laboratorio del jueves y ella acepta ("Please do that"). B y D contradicen "You can"; C no se propone.

screen.title: Academic Talk: How migrating birds find their way
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.

audio.text: Every autumn, millions of songbirds fly thousands of kilometers to their wintering grounds, and many of them travel at night, alone, on their very first journey. So how do they know which way to go? It turns out they don't rely on a single cue. They carry what amounts to several compasses.

One is the sun. Birds that fly by day can judge direction from the sun's position, adjusting for the time of day. Night migrants need something else, and a classic experiment revealed what it was. Researchers raised young birds in a planetarium, under an artificial sky that rotated around a different star than the real North Star. When migration season arrived, the birds oriented themselves using that false center of rotation. In other words, they had learned the pattern of the sky; they hadn't inherited a map of particular stars.

Birds also sense the Earth's magnetic field. Interestingly, their magnetic compass doesn't distinguish north from south the way ours does. Instead, it detects the angle at which the field lines dip toward the ground, which tells a bird whether it's heading toward the pole or toward the equator. And on overcast nights, when the stars disappear, that magnetic sense appears to keep them on course.

questions.stem: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: Why songbirds prefer to migrate at night rather than by day
The different cues birds use to orient themselves during migration
How planetariums are used to teach university students about the night sky
Why young birds follow older birds on long journeys

why.en: Main idea: birds use several "compasses" (the sun, the stars, the magnetic field). D contradicts "alone, on their very first journey"; C turns the setting of the experiment into the topic.
why.tr: Ana fikir: kuşlar birkaç "pusula" kullanır (güneş, yıldızlar, manyetik alan). D "alone, on their very first journey" ile çelişiyor; C deneyin yapıldığı yeri konu hâline getiriyor.
why.es: Idea principal: las aves usan varias "brújulas" (el sol, las estrellas, el campo magnético). D contradice "alone, on their very first journey"; C convierte el lugar del experimento en el tema.

questions.stem: What did the planetarium experiment show?
options: Birds lose their sense of direction completely when the sky rotates
Birds prefer artificial light to real starlight
Night migrants depend mainly on the position of the sun
Young birds learn the sky's pattern instead of inheriting it

why.en: Detail/inference: the birds used the false center of rotation, so they "had learned the pattern of the sky". A contradicts the result (they oriented themselves successfully); C applies to day migrants.
why.tr: Ayrıntı/çıkarım: kuşlar sahte dönme merkezini kullandı, yani "had learned the pattern of the sky". A sonuçla çelişiyor (kuşlar yönlerini buldu); C gündüz göç eden kuşlar için geçerli.
why.es: Detalle/inferencia: las aves usaron el falso centro de rotación, así que "had learned the pattern of the sky". A contradice el resultado (se orientaron sin problema); C se aplica a las aves que migran de día.

questions.stem: According to the professor, what does a bird's magnetic compass detect?
options: The angle at which the field lines meet the ground
The difference between magnetic north and south
The direction in which the night sky rotates
The distance remaining to the bird's wintering grounds

why.en: Detail: it "detects the angle at which the field lines dip toward the ground". B is exactly what the professor says it does not do; C belongs to the star compass.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: "detects the angle at which the field lines dip toward the ground". B profesörün tam olarak yapmadığını söylediği şey; C yıldız pusulasına ait.
why.es: Detalle: "detects the angle at which the field lines dip toward the ground". B es justo lo que la profesora dice que no hace; C corresponde a la brújula estelar.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about a night migrant flying under heavy cloud?
options: It must land until the stars return

why.en: Inference: on overcast nights the magnetic sense "appears to keep them on course". A contradicts that; B is impossible at night.
why.tr: Çıkarım: kapalı gecelerde manyetik duyu "appears to keep them on course". A bununla çelişiyor; B gece mümkün değil.
why.es: Inferencia: en noches nubladas, el sentido magnético "appears to keep them on course". A lo contradice; B es imposible de noche.

screen.prompt: Listen to part of a talk in a history class.

audio.text: Today let's talk about farming on steep hills. Farming on a slope is hard. When it rains, water runs down the hill very fast, and it carries the good soil away with it. So, thousands of years ago, farmers in many mountain areas found a clever answer. They built terraces. A terrace is a flat step cut into the side of a hill, usually held up by a low stone wall. A hill with terraces looks like a giant staircase. On each flat step, rainwater slows down and sinks into the ground, and the soil stays in place. Farmers grew rice, potatoes, and many other crops this way. Some of these old terraces are still used today.

why.es: Idea principal: las terrazas resolvieron el problema de cultivar en pendiente. C toma "giant staircase" al pie de la letra; B usa mal "stone wall".

screen.title: Academic Talk: From harpsichord to piano
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a music history class.

audio.text: Today I want to look at an instrument you all know, the piano, and why it was such an important change. Before about 1700, the main keyboard instrument in Europe was the harpsichord. When you press a key on a harpsichord, a small quill called a plectrum plucks the string. The problem is that the plectrum plucks it in the same way no matter how hard you press, so a player can't make one note louder than another.

Around 1700, an instrument maker in Florence, Bartolomeo Cristofori, replaced the plectrum with a small hammer that strikes the string and then falls away. Press the key gently and the hammer hits softly; press it hard and the note is loud. That's where the name comes from: pianoforte means soft-loud in Italian.

Interestingly, the new instrument didn't catch on right away. Early pianos were quiet and expensive, and many musicians saw no reason to give up the harpsichord. It took several decades before composers began writing music that depended on gradual changes in volume. Then, in the nineteenth century, builders added iron frames, which could hold thicker strings under much greater tension. Pianos became loud enough to fill large concert halls, and that's the instrument we recognize today.

questions.stem: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: The development of a keyboard that could play softly or loudly
Why many performers today still prefer the harpsichord to the piano
How concert halls in Florence were designed for music
The life and work of a famous composer of the 1700s

why.en: Main idea: how the piano solved the harpsichord's volume problem and later grew louder. B reverses the direction of the lecture; C misuses "Florence", where the inventor worked.
why.tr: Ana fikir: piyanonun klavsenin ses şiddeti sorununu nasıl çözdüğü ve sonra nasıl daha güçlü hâle geldiği. B dersin yönünü tersine çeviriyor; C mucidin çalıştığı yer olan "Florence" kelimesini yanlış kullanıyor.
why.es: Idea principal: cómo el piano resolvió el problema de volumen del clavecín y después ganó potencia. B invierte el sentido de la clase; C usa mal "Florence", donde trabajaba el inventor.

questions.stem: According to the professor, what was the main limitation of the harpsichord?
options: Its strings often broke when the keys were pressed hard
It was much too loud for small rooms in private homes
Players could not make some notes louder than others
Its hammers fell away from the strings too quickly

why.en: Detail: the plectrum plucks the string "in the same way no matter how hard you press". D gives the harpsichord the piano's hammers; A is never mentioned.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: kanca teli "in the same way no matter how hard you press" çekiyor. D piyanonun çekiçlerini klavsene mal ediyor; A hiç söylenmiyor.
why.es: Detalle: el gancho pulsa la cuerda "in the same way no matter how hard you press". D atribuye al clavecín los martillos del piano; A nunca se menciona.

questions.stem: Why does the professor explain the meaning of the word "pianoforte"?
options: To prove that the piano was invented by an Italian composer
To explain why early pianos were so expensive to build
To introduce a second instrument made in Florence
To show that the name describes what the instrument could do

why.en: Purpose: "soft-loud" names exactly the new ability to vary the volume. A turns the instrument maker into a composer; B links the name to a different point.
why.tr: Amaç: "soft-loud", ses şiddetini değiştirme yeteneğini tam olarak adlandırıyor. A çalgı yapımcısını besteciye dönüştürüyor; B adı başka bir noktaya bağlıyor.
why.es: Propósito: "soft-loud" nombra justo la nueva capacidad de variar el volumen. A convierte al fabricante de instrumentos en compositor; B relaciona el nombre con otro punto.

questions.stem: What does the professor imply about nineteenth-century pianos?
options: They cost much less to build than the earliest pianos did
They could be heard clearly in big performance spaces
They went back to using plectrums instead of hammers
They were played mostly in small private homes

why.en: Inference from "loud enough to fill large concert halls". D contradicts that point; C reverses the history of the mechanism.
why.tr: "Loud enough to fill large concert halls" ifadesinden çıkarım. D bununla çelişiyor; C mekanizmanın tarihini tersine çeviriyor.
why.es: Inferencia a partir de "loud enough to fill large concert halls". D contradice esa idea; C invierte la historia del mecanismo.

screen.title: Academic Talk: Finding planets around other stars
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an astronomy class.

audio.text: Planets orbiting other stars are extremely hard to see directly. A star is billions of times brighter than any planet near it, so the planet's faint light is simply lost in the glare. Instead, astronomers usually detect these planets indirectly, and today the most productive approach is called the transit method.

Here's the idea. If a planet's orbit happens to be lined up with our line of sight, then once per orbit the planet passes in front of its star. When that happens, it blocks a tiny fraction of the starlight, often less than one percent. A sensitive telescope that measures the star's brightness continuously will record a small, regular dip. The time between dips tells us the length of the planet's year, and the depth of each dip tells us how large the planet is compared with its star.

Now, a single dip doesn't prove anything. Stars have dark spots, and a second star passing in front can produce a similar signal. That's why astronomers want to see at least three evenly spaced dips before they take a candidate seriously. And keep in mind the method's built-in bias: it only finds systems whose orbits we happen to see edge-on, so for every planet detected this way, many more must be passing by unseen.

questions.stem: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: Why some stars shine much more brightly than others
How telescopes take direct photographs of distant planets
Detecting distant planets by measuring changes in starlight
Why the planets that orbit other stars have such short years

why.en: Main idea: the transit method, its logic and its limits. B contradicts the opening point that such planets are "extremely hard to see directly".
why.tr: Ana fikir: geçiş yöntemi, mantığı ve sınırları. B bu gezegenlerin "extremely hard to see directly" olduğu yönündeki açılış bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Idea principal: el método de tránsito, su lógica y sus límites. B contradice la idea inicial de que estos planetas son "extremely hard to see directly".

questions.stem: According to the professor, what does the depth of a dip reveal?
options: The planet's size relative to its star
The length of the planet's year
The planet's distance from Earth
The temperature of the planet

why.en: Detail: "the depth of each dip tells us how large the planet is compared with its star". B is what the time between dips shows, the classic swap.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: "the depth of each dip tells us how large the planet is compared with its star". B düşüşler arasındaki sürenin gösterdiği şey; klasik yer değiştirme tuzağı.
why.es: Detalle: "the depth of each dip tells us how large the planet is compared with its star". B es lo que indica el tiempo entre caídas: la trampa clásica del intercambio.

questions.stem: Why does the professor mention dark spots on stars?
options: To show how stars lose brightness as they grow older
To explain why one dip cannot confirm a planet
To describe a feature that makes planets easier to see
To compare the size of the spots with that of planets

why.en: Purpose: spots, like a second star, can imitate a dip, so "a single dip doesn't prove anything". C reverses their role, since they are a source of false signals.
why.tr: Amaç: lekeler, tıpkı ikinci bir yıldız gibi, düşüşü taklit edebilir; bu yüzden "a single dip doesn't prove anything". C rollerini tersine çeviriyor, çünkü lekeler yanıltıcı sinyal kaynağı.
why.es: Propósito: las manchas, como una segunda estrella, pueden imitar una caída, así que "a single dip doesn't prove anything". C invierte su papel, porque son una fuente de señales falsas.

questions.stem: What does the professor imply about the planets found with the transit method?
options: They all orbit stars that are covered with dark spots
They are the largest planets in our galaxy
They can also be seen directly with telescopes
They are only a small share of the planets that exist

why.en: Inference from "for every planet detected this way, many more must be passing by unseen". C contradicts the opening of the lecture; A misuses the point about dark spots, which can only imitate a planet's signal.
why.tr: "For every planet detected this way, many more must be passing by unseen" ifadesinden çıkarım. C dersin girişiyle çelişiyor; A yalnızca gezegen sinyalini taklit edebilen karanlık lekelerle ilgili bilgiyi yanlış kullanıyor.
why.es: Inferencia a partir de "for every planet detected this way, many more must be passing by unseen". C contradice el inicio de la clase; A usa mal lo dicho sobre las manchas oscuras, que solo pueden imitar la señal de un planeta.

screen.title: Academic Talk: How island chains form
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a talk in a geology class.

audio.text: Today let's look at how some chains of volcanic islands form. Deep under certain parts of the ocean floor, there are very hot places called hot spots. Melted rock, called magma, rises from a hot spot and breaks through the ocean floor, building a volcano. If the volcano grows tall enough, it becomes an island. But the plate of rock that makes up the ocean floor moves slowly, a few centimeters a year, while the hot spot stays in one place. So, over millions of years, the island is carried away from the hot spot, its volcano stops erupting, and a new volcano starts to grow behind it. That's why the islands in a chain get older as you move along it.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?
options: Why volcanoes erupt more often in the ocean
How scientists measure the age of rocks
Why islands slowly sink into the sea
How a hot spot can create a line of islands

why.en: Main idea: one hot spot builds island after island as the plate moves. C and A are not discussed; B is not explained in the talk.
why.tr: Ana fikir: levha hareket ettikçe tek bir sıcak nokta art arda adalar oluşturur. C ve A konuşmada yok; B konuşmada anlatılmıyor.
why.es: Idea principal: un solo punto caliente forma una isla tras otra a medida que se mueve la placa. C y A no se tratan; B no se explica en la charla.

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what moves?
options: The hot spot itself
The water around the islands
The plate of rock under the ocean
The level of the sea

why.en: Detail: the plate "moves slowly … while the hot spot stays in one place". A is the trap: it reverses what moves and what stays still.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: levha "moves slowly … while the hot spot stays in one place". A tuzak: neyin hareket ettiğini ve neyin sabit kaldığını tersine çeviriyor.
why.es: Detalle: la placa "moves slowly … while the hot spot stays in one place". A es la trampa: invierte qué se mueve y qué se queda quieto.

questions.stem: What happens when an island is carried away from the hot spot?
options: It becomes taller and wider
Its volcano stops erupting
It joins with another island
A new hot spot forms under it

why.en: Detail: "its volcano stops erupting". D is wrong because the new volcano grows over the same hot spot, not under the old island; A is the opposite of what happens.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: "its volcano stops erupting". D yanlış, çünkü yeni yanardağ eski adanın altında değil, aynı sıcak noktanın üzerinde oluşuyor; A olanın tam tersi.
why.es: Detalle: "its volcano stops erupting". D es incorrecta porque el nuevo volcán crece sobre el mismo punto caliente, no bajo la isla vieja; A es lo contrario de lo que ocurre.

questions.stem: Where is the youngest island in a chain probably found?
options: Closest to the hot spot
At the end farthest from the hot spot
In the middle of the chain
Where the plate is thickest

why.en: Inference: islands get older as they move away, so the newest one is the one still over the hot spot. B is the trap: the far end holds the oldest islands.
why.tr: Çıkarım: adalar uzaklaştıkça yaşlanıyor; demek ki en genç ada hâlâ sıcak noktanın üzerinde olandır. B tuzak: zincirin öbür ucunda en yaşlı adalar var.
why.es: Inferencia: las islas envejecen a medida que se alejan, así que la más joven es la que sigue sobre el punto caliente. B es la trampa: en el otro extremo están las islas más antiguas.

screen.title: Academic Talk: Why wider roads fill up
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an urban planning class.

audio.text: Today I want to look at a puzzle that city planners have struggled with for decades. When a highway is crowded, the obvious solution seems to be adding more lanes. More space for cars should mean less traffic, right? Yet study after study has found that within a few years, the widened road is often just as crowded as before.

Planners call this induced demand. When driving becomes faster and easier, people change their behavior. Someone who used to take the train starts driving instead. Someone who avoided rush hour starts leaving at eight rather than seven. Some families even move farther out, because the commute now seems manageable. All these small decisions add up to more cars, until traffic is back where it started. Some studies have even found that traffic grows almost exactly in step with the amount of new road space.

Now, this doesn't mean new roads are never useful. A road linking two towns that had no direct connection can make a real difference. But for busy routes inside a city, many planners now argue it's better to manage demand, for example by charging drivers to enter crowded areas at peak hours, or by improving bus service so that fewer people need to drive.

questions.stem: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: How highways were first designed in large cities
Why trains are faster than cars at rush hour
Why adding road space often fails to reduce traffic
How families decide where to live in a city

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase of induced demand): widened roads soon fill up again. B and D take small examples from the lecture and make them the topic; A is never discussed.
why.tr: Ana fikir ("induced demand" kavramının parafrazı): genişletilen yollar kısa sürede yeniden doluyor. B ve D konuşmadaki küçük örnekleri ana konu yapıyor; A hiç ele alınmıyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis de "induced demand"): las carreteras ampliadas pronto vuelven a llenarse. B y D toman ejemplos pequeños de la clase y los convierten en el tema; A no se trata.

questions.stem: According to the professor, how do some people respond when a highway becomes faster?
options: They sell their cars and start cycling to work
They travel at times they used to avoid
They complain to the city about road charges
They move closer to the city center

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): someone who "avoided rush hour starts leaving at eight". D reverses the example, since families move farther out, not closer; A is the opposite of what she describes.
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): "avoided rush hour" olan biri artık saat sekizde yola çıkıyor. D örneği tersine çeviriyor, çünkü aileler merkeze yaklaşmıyor, uzaklaşıyor; A anlatılanın tam tersi.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): alguien que "avoided rush hour" empieza a salir a las ocho. D invierte el ejemplo, porque las familias se van más lejos, no más cerca; A es lo contrario de lo que ella describe.

questions.stem: Why does the professor mention a road linking two towns?
options: To show that induced demand affects small towns most
To describe a road that later became very crowded
To explain how the idea of induced demand began
To give an example of when building a road can help

screen.title: Academic Talk: When children say "goed"
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a linguistics class.

audio.text: Here's something parents often notice. A two-year-old correctly says "I went" or "two feet." Then, a few months later, the same child starts saying "I goed" and "two foots." It looks as if the child's language is getting worse. In fact, it's a sign of progress. Let me explain why.

Linguists call these errors overregularization. At first, children seem to learn each past-tense form as a separate word, simply by copying what they hear. "Went" is just another word. But as their vocabulary grows, they begin to notice a pattern: most English verbs form the past by adding "-ed." Once they've worked out that rule, they apply it everywhere, even to irregular verbs they used to get right. The same thing happens with plurals, which is where "foots" comes from.

The key point is that children almost never hear forms like "goed" from adults. So they can't be imitating. They're producing something new from a rule they've discovered on their own. Eventually, with enough exposure, the correct irregular forms come back, and the rule is used only where it belongs. Researchers call this U-shaped development: performance starts high, drops, and then recovers, and the dip in the middle actually reflects deeper learning.

options: Why parents should correct children's grammar mistakes

why.tr: Ana fikir: aşırı düzenlileştirme (overregularization) hataları çocukların bir kural öğrendiğini gösteriyor. A konuşmada hiç önerilmiyor; B konuyu yetişkinlere kaydırıyor; C ele alınmıyor.
why.es: Idea principal: los errores de sobrerregularización muestran que los niños han aprendido una regla. A no se recomienda en ningún momento; B cambia el tema a los adultos; C no se trata.

screen.title: Academic Talk: Cooling buildings with wind catchers
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an architecture class.

audio.text: Long before air conditioning, builders in hot, dry regions found ways to keep interiors comfortable. One of the most elegant is the wind catcher, a tall tower rising above the roof, which you can still see in parts of Iran and around the Persian Gulf. Near the top, the tower has openings that face the prevailing wind.

The basic principle is simple. Wind enters the openings and is pushed down a shaft into the rooms below, while warm indoor air escapes through windows or another part of the tower. Moving air feels cooler on the skin, even when its temperature doesn't change. But many wind catchers went further. Some sent the incoming air over a pool of water or through an underground channel before it reached the living spaces. As the water evaporated, it absorbed heat, so the air arriving inside really was several degrees cooler.

Interestingly, wind catchers can work even on still days. The tower's walls soak up sunlight, so the air inside the shaft warms up and rises, pulling fresh air through the house behind it. In other words, the tower acts as both a scoop and a chimney. Today, some architects are returning to the design, since it cools buildings without using any electricity.

options: Why buildings in dry regions were built without windows

why.tr: Ana fikir: rüzgâr kulelerinin alttaki odaları nasıl serinlettiği. A konuşmayla çelişiyor, çünkü sıcak hava pencerelerden çıkıyor; D tek bir serinletme yöntemini ana konu yapıyor; C yalnızca karşılaştırma için anılıyor.
why.es: Idea principal: cómo las torres de viento refrescan las habitaciones de abajo. A contradice la clase, porque el aire caliente sale por las ventanas; D convierte una sola técnica de refrigeración en el tema; C solo se menciona como contraste.

why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): "As the water evaporated, it absorbed heat", así que el aire estaba realmente más fresco. C lo confunde con la idea distinta de que el aire en movimiento solo se siente más fresco; A y B no se mencionan.

audio.text: Beavers are famous for building dams across small rivers. They use sticks, mud and stones to block the water, and a pond forms behind the dam. screen.title: Academic Talk: How fog forms
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a meteorology class.

audio.text: Today let's talk about fog, which is really just a cloud that forms at ground level. Fog appears when the air near the ground cools until it can't hold all of its water vapor, so the extra vapor condenses into tiny droplets. One common type is radiation fog. On clear, calm nights, the ground loses heat quickly into the sky, and it cools the air just above it. By early morning, valleys can fill with fog, because cold air is heavier and collects in low places. Once the sun warms the ground, this kind of fog usually disappears by midmorning.

A second type, advection fog, forms in a different way. Here, warm, moist air moves across a cold surface, such as a cold ocean current. The air is cooled from below, and fog develops even when it's windy. That's why some coastal cities can be foggy for days in summer, when the land is hot but the water offshore stays cold. So if you want to predict fog, don't just look at the temperature. Look at the wind, the sky, and the kind of surface the air is moving over.

screen.title: Academic Talk: What ice cores record
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an earth science class.

audio.text: When snow falls on a large ice sheet, such as the one covering Antarctica, it doesn't melt. Year after year, new layers pile up, and the weight of the snow above slowly presses the older layers into solid ice. As this happens, tiny bubbles of air become trapped inside. Those bubbles are, in effect, samples of the atmosphere from the time the snow fell.

By drilling deep into the ice and pulling out long cylinders, which we call ice cores, researchers can measure what the air contained thousands of years ago. The deepest Antarctic cores reach back roughly eight hundred thousand years. Scientists can also estimate past temperatures from the chemistry of the ice itself, since snow that falls in colder periods contains a slightly different mix of oxygen atoms.

Now, the method has limits. Near the surface, the snow hasn't sealed yet, so air can still move between the layers. This means the air in a bubble is always somewhat younger than the ice around it, sometimes by thousands of years, and researchers have to correct for that gap before they compare the two records.

screen.title: Academic Talk: Why early photos look empty
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a history of photography class.

audio.text: Let's look at one of the earliest photographs of people, taken in Paris in 1838 by Louis Daguerre. It shows a boulevard that was normally full of traffic, yet the street appears almost empty. The reason is the exposure time. Daguerre's plates needed several minutes of light to record an image, so anything that moved, such as carriages or people walking, simply didn't stay in one place long enough to appear.

There's one exception, though, and it's easy to miss. In the lower corner, you can make out a man who seems to be having his boots polished. Because he stood still for minutes, he became, quite by accident, one of the first people ever photographed.

Long exposures shaped early portrait photography too. Sitters had to hold their position for a long time, and studios used hidden metal stands to support their heads. This is one reason people in early portraits rarely smile: holding a natural smile for that long is almost impossible. As the chemistry improved over the following decades, exposure times dropped to a few seconds, and photographers could finally capture busy streets as they really looked.

screen.title: Academic Talk: How bats hunt in the dark
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.

audio.text: Today let's look at how bats find their way in complete darkness. Most bats rely on a process called echolocation. A bat produces a series of very high-pitched calls, usually too high for humans to hear, and then listens for the echoes that bounce back from objects around it. By noticing how long each echo takes to return, the bat can judge how far away an object is, and differences between what its two ears hear tell it the direction.

Now, here's what I find remarkable. When a bat is simply flying across open space, it might call around ten times per second. But as it closes in on an insect, the rate rises sharply, to well over a hundred calls per second. Researchers call this final burst the feeding buzz. The faster calls give the bat almost continuous updates about the insect's position, which matters because the insect is moving too.

Some moths, by the way, have evolved a defense. They can hear bat calls, and when they detect one, they suddenly drop or change direction. A few species even produce clicks of their own that seem to interfere with the bat's signal. So this is really an ongoing contest between hunter and prey.

screen.title: Academic Talk: The rise of linear perspective
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an art history class.

audio.text: Let's turn to one of the great technical advances of the Renaissance: linear perspective. Before the fifteenth century, European painters certainly suggested depth. They placed distant figures higher in the picture or made them smaller, but they lacked a consistent system, and different objects in the same painting often seemed to recede at different angles.

In Florence, early in the fifteenth century, the architect Filippo Brunelleschi carried out a famous demonstration. He painted a small panel showing the city's baptistery and drilled a hole through it. A viewer looked through the hole from the back while holding a mirror in front of the panel, so the reflected painting could be compared directly with the real building. The two lined up remarkably well.

The principle behind this is that parallel lines moving away from the viewer appear to meet at a single point, which we now call the vanishing point. In the 1430s, Leon Battista Alberti described the method in writing, which allowed it to spread far beyond Brunelleschi's circle. Keep in mind, though, that perspective wasn't only about accuracy. Painters used the vanishing point to guide the viewer's eye, often toward the most important figure in the scene.

screen.title: Academic Talk: Path dependence
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an economics class.

audio.text: Let's talk about a concept economists call path dependence. The basic idea is that decisions made in the past can limit the choices available today, even when the original reasons no longer apply.

The classic example is the keyboard layout most of you are using right now, known as QWERTY. It was designed in the 1870s for mechanical typewriters. One popular explanation is that it placed common letter pairs apart so the metal arms wouldn't jam, although historians still argue about how much that really mattered. Either way, the jamming problem disappeared long ago. Other layouts have been designed since then. The Dvorak keyboard, for example, put the most common letters on the middle row, where your fingers already rest, and some people claim it's faster. Yet QWERTY is everywhere.

Why? Because once millions of people had learned it, and schools taught it, and manufacturers produced it, switching became very costly. A new layout would have to be better by enough to make everyone relearn typing at the same time. So the old standard survives, not necessarily because it's the best, but because everyone else is already using it. And economists find the same pattern whenever the value of a choice depends on what everyone else has already chosen.

screen.title: Academic Talk: Managing shared resources
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an economics class.

audio.text: In economics there's a well-known idea called the tragedy of the commons. Picture a pasture that everyone in a village may use. Each herder reasons that adding one more cow brings him the full benefit of that cow, while the cost, slightly less grass, is shared by everyone. So each herder adds cows, and eventually the pasture is ruined, even though no one wanted that outcome.

For a long time, economists assumed there were only two solutions: either the government controls the resource, or it's divided into private property. But the political economist Elinor Ostrom challenged that view. She studied fisheries, forests, and irrigation systems around the world that communities had managed successfully for centuries without either solution.

What did those communities have in common? Ostrom found that they set clear boundaries around who could use the resource, they made their own rules about how much each person could take, and, this is important, they monitored one another and applied gradually increasing penalties to people who broke the rules. In 2009 she became the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in economics, partly for this work. So the lesson isn't that shared resources are always doomed. It's that the outcome depends on how the users organize themselves.
