screen.title: Academic Talk: The serial position effect
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a talk in a psychology class.

audio.text: Today I want to talk about something you've probably experienced without realizing it. Imagine I read you a list of twenty words and then ask you to write down as many as you can remember. Most people recall the first few words and the last few words quite well, but the words in the middle tend to disappear. Psychologists call this the serial position effect.

So why does it happen? The words at the beginning get more rehearsal. When you hear the first word, you repeat it to yourself a few times, and that repetition helps move it into long-term memory. By the time the middle of the list arrives, you're trying to rehearse many words at once, so each one gets less attention. The words at the end are a different story. They're still sitting in short-term memory when you start writing, so you can simply read them off, so to speak.

Here's the interesting part. If I make you wait thirty seconds and count backward before you write, the advantage for the final words disappears, but the advantage for the first words remains. That tells us two different memory systems are involved. So, practically speaking, when you study, try not to always start from the same page. Otherwise the middle chapters will always get the least attention.

screen.title: Academic Talk: The wolves of Yellowstone
screen.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an environmental science class.

audio.text: In 1995, wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone National Park after an absence of about seventy years. What happened next became one of the most famous stories in ecology. Without wolves, elk had grazed freely along the rivers, eating young willow and aspen trees before they could grow. Once wolves returned, the story goes, elk began avoiding open river valleys where they could easily be hunted. The trees recovered, beavers returned to use the wood, and their dams created ponds that supported fish and birds. Ecologists call a chain of effects like this a trophic cascade.

Now, it's a great story, and parts of it are clearly true. But more recent research suggests the picture is messier. Elk numbers also fell because of hunting by people, harsh winters, and a growing population of bears. And in some areas the willows haven't recovered at all, because without beaver dams the water table had dropped too low for the trees to grow back. In other words, removing a predator can trigger changes that simply adding it back doesn't reverse.
So what's the lesson? Not that the wolves didn't matter. They did. The lesson is that ecosystems don't always work like a light switch. Restoring one species is often only the first step.

screen.title: Color Words and Perception
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — upper module
text: Languages differ considerably in how they divide the color spectrum. Russian, for instance, obligatorily distinguishes between lighter blues (goluboy) and darker blues (siniy), whereas English speakers use a single basic term. This raises a question that has long intrigued linguists and psychologists: does the vocabulary a person habitually uses shape the way that person actually perceives the world?

Experimental evidence suggests a modest but measurable influence. In one study, Russian speakers distinguished between two shades of blue more rapidly when the shades straddled the boundary between goluboy and siniy than when both fell within a single category; English speakers showed no comparable advantage. Crucially, the effect vanished when participants simultaneously performed a verbal task that occupied their linguistic resources.

Researchers therefore caution against strong claims. Language does not appear to determine what people are capable of seeing; it seems instead to provide a convenient shortcut that accelerates certain judgments whenever linguistic processing is available.

screen.title: Underground Fungal Networks
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — upper module
text: Beneath most forests lies an extensive web of fungal threads known as mycorrhizal networks. These fungi colonize the roots of trees, supplying them with water and mineral nutrients such as phosphorus in exchange for sugars that the trees produce through photosynthesis.

Because a single network can connect the roots of many different trees, researchers have proposed that carbon and other resources may travel from one tree to another through these shared connections. Some experiments have reported that seedlings growing in deep shade receive carbon from larger neighbors, which might improve their chances of survival.

Nevertheless, the more dramatic claims, for instance that mature trees deliberately nurture their offspring or warn neighbors of insect attacks, remain contested. Critics note that many field studies were small, that the direction of transfer is difficult to measure, and that fungi may move resources primarily for their own benefit rather than for that of the forest.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How fungi harm the roots of young trees
Evidence about a forest-wide exchange system and its limits
The way trees warn one another of insect attacks
Methods for growing seedlings in deep shade

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): the networks, what they may do, and doubts about the strongest claims. C treats a contested claim as fact.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): ağlar, ne yapıyor olabilecekleri ve en iddialı yorumlara dair şüpheler. C tartışmalı bir iddiayı gerçek gibi sunuyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): las redes, lo que podrían hacer y las dudas sobre las afirmaciones más fuertes. C trata una afirmación discutida como un hecho.

questions.stem: The word "contested" in the passage is closest in meaning to

why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: contested claims = afirmaciones que se discuten.

why.en: Author's purpose: an experimental result supporting transfer. A overstates it — the author says that claim remains contested.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: kaynak aktarımını destekleyen bir deney sonucu. A abartıyor; yazar bu iddianın tartışmalı olduğunu söylüyor.
why.es: Propósito del autor: un resultado experimental que apoya la transferencia. A lo exagera: el autor dice que esa afirmación sigue en discusión.

why.en: Inference: the critics' points (small studies, hard measurement, fungi's own benefit) imply the claims exceed the evidence. A contradicts "many field studies were small".
why.tr: Çıkarım: eleştiriler (küçük çalışmalar, ölçüm zorluğu, mantarların kendi çıkarı) iddiaların kanıtı aştığını gösteriyor. A "çalışmaların çoğu küçüktü" bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: los puntos de los críticos (estudios pequeños, medición difícil, el propio beneficio de los hongos) implican que las afirmaciones superan las pruebas. A contradice "many field studies were small".

questions.stem: According to the passage, what do trees provide to the fungi?
options: Water absorbed from the soil
Sugars made through photosynthesis

why.en: Detail: fungi get "sugars that the trees produce through photosynthesis". A and C are what the fungi give the trees — the direction trap.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: mantarlar "ağaçların fotosentezle ürettiği şekerleri" alır. A ve C mantarların ağaçlara verdikleri — yön tuzağı.
why.es: Detalle: los hongos reciben "sugars that the trees produce through photosynthesis". A y C son lo que los hongos dan a los árboles: la trampa de la dirección.

screen.title: The Invention of Standard Time
text: Until the late nineteenth century, most towns set their clocks by the sun. Noon was the moment when the sun stood highest in the sky, so the time in one city could differ by several minutes from the time in a city a short distance to the east or west.

This local system caused few problems while travel was slow. The arrival of railroads, however, changed the situation. Each railway company kept its own schedule, and a single station might display several clocks showing different times. Passengers often missed connections.

In 1883, railroads in the United States and Canada adopted a system of time zones, each differing from its neighbor by exactly one hour. Many communities at first resisted giving up "sun time," but the convenience of the new system gradually won acceptance.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why railroad companies charged different prices
Why people preferred sun time to railroad time
How faster travel led to a shared way of keeping time
How engineers built more accurate clocks

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase). B reverses the outcome; A and D are not discussed.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz). B sonucu tersine çeviriyor; A ve D metinde yok.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis). B invierte el resultado; A y D no se tratan.

why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: adopted a system = empezó a usarlo.

why.es: Inferencia a partir de "caused few problems while travel was slow". C invierte la dirección; D no se dice.

why.es: Detalle: "each differing from its neighbor by exactly one hour". D contradice "at first resisted".

screen.title: Urban Heat Islands
text: On a summer afternoon, the center of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the countryside around it. Scientists call this an urban heat island. The main cause is the material that cities are built from: asphalt, concrete and brick absorb sunlight during the day and slowly release that heat at night.

Cities also lack the natural cooling that plants provide. Trees shade the ground, and they release water vapor through their leaves, which cools the surrounding air in much the same way that sweat cools skin. Where green spaces are replaced by roads and buildings, this effect disappears.

The consequences go beyond discomfort. Warmer nights prevent people from recovering from daytime heat, and heat waves in cities are linked to more hospital visits. Some cities now paint roofs white, plant trees along streets and build parks, and early results suggest that these simple changes can lower local temperatures noticeably.

why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis). B y A confunden detalles (materiales, sudor) con el todo.

screen.title: Why Cats Purr
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — lower module
text: Cats purr when they are happy, but that is not the only reason. A cat may also purr when it is hurt, hungry or scared. Mother cats purr to their kittens, and kittens purr back to show that they are fine.

Some scientists think purring helps cats calm down. Others believe the low sound may even help bones and muscles heal faster. Cats make the sound by moving muscles in their throat very quickly as they breathe in and out.
Even after many studies, scientists still do not fully agree on why cats purr.

screen.title: Light in the Ocean
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — lower module
text: Sunlight does not go very deep into the ocean. Scientists divide the ocean into zones based on how much light reaches them. The top zone, down to about 200 meters, gets plenty of sunlight. Most sea plants and many fish live there.

Below that is the twilight zone. Only a little blue light reaches it, and plants cannot grow there. Deeper still, below 1,000 meters, the water is completely dark. Many animals in this deep zone make their own light. They use it to find food, to attract partners, or to confuse enemies.

screen.title: The Three-Field System
text: For many centuries, farmers across much of Europe divided their land into two large fields. Each year, one field was planted with grain, while the other was deliberately left unplanted, or fallow, so that the soil could recover its natural fertility. This method protected the soil, but it meant that half of the available land produced nothing in any given year.

Around the eighth century, many villages began organizing their land into three fields instead. One field was sown with wheat or rye in the autumn, a second was planted in spring with oats, peas, or beans, and the third was allowed to rest. The crops then rotated to a different field each year.

This change brought two significant advantages. First, two-thirds of the land was now under cultivation at any time. Second, peas and beans naturally return nitrogen to the soil, so the fields remained productive for longer. The additional oats also supported more horses, which could plow considerably faster than oxen.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why European farmers stopped growing wheat and rye
A new way of farming that made fields more productive
How horses gradually replaced oxen on farms across Europe
Why fallow fields produced the largest harvests

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): the move from two fields to three and its advantages. C turns a minor detail into the main topic; A and D contradict the passage.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): iki tarladan üç tarlaya geçiş ve faydaları. C küçük bir ayrıntıyı ana konu yapıyor; A ve D metinle çelişiyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): el paso de dos campos a tres y sus ventajas. C convierte un detalle menor en el tema principal; A y D contradicen el texto.

protect

why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: el campo descansaba para que la tierra pudiera "recover" (recuperar) su fertilidad natural. B toma prestado "protected" de la frase siguiente.

why.tr: Yazarın amacı: cümle, iki tarla sisteminin bedelini gösteriyor; üç tarla sistemi bu bedeli sonradan azalttı. D aşırıya kaçıyor, çünkü bir tarla yine dinlendiriliyordu; C bu noktayı sonraki ilgisiz bir ayrıntıya bağlıyor.

screen.title: The Strength of Weak Ties
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — upper module
text: Sociologists distinguish between strong ties, such as those connecting close friends and relatives, and weak ties, which link acquaintances who interact only occasionally. Intuitively, one might assume that strong ties constitute the more valuable resource, since close contacts are typically more willing to offer assistance.

A frequently cited study of professional workers, however, found that people who had obtained jobs through personal contacts more often heard about the position from acquaintances than from close friends. The explanation proposed was structural: members of a tightly knit circle tend to know the same people and encounter the same information, whereas acquaintances move in different social circles and can therefore transmit news that would otherwise remain inaccessible.

Subsequent research has qualified this conclusion. Strong ties appear more influential when information is scarce or when a recommendation requires considerable trust, and the advantage of weak ties seems to depend on the type of labor market. Nevertheless, the central insight, that the value of a connection lies partly in the novelty of what it can provide, has proved remarkably durable.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A finding about the value of distant contacts and later limits on it
How professional workers can turn their acquaintances into close friends
Why strong ties always outperform weak ties during a job search
The research methods that sociologists use to measure friendship

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): the weak-ties finding, its explanation and the later qualifications. C contradicts the study; B invents a topic the passage never discusses.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): zayıf bağlar bulgusu, açıklaması ve sonradan getirilen sınırlamalar. C çalışmayla çelişiyor; B metinde hiç ele alınmayan bir konu uyduruyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): el hallazgo sobre los lazos débiles, su explicación y los matices posteriores. C contradice el estudio; B se inventa un tema que el texto nunca trata.

questions.stem: The word "qualified" in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: certified
confirmed
rejected
limited

why.en: Vocabulary in context: later research "qualified" the conclusion, i.e. limited it by adding conditions. A is another meaning of "qualified" that does not fit here; C is too strong, because the central insight survived.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: sonraki araştırmalar sonucu "qualified" etti, yani koşullar ekleyerek sınırladı. A "qualified" kelimesinin buraya uymayan başka bir anlamı; C fazla güçlü, çünkü temel fikir geçerliliğini korudu.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: la investigación posterior "qualified" la conclusión, es decir, la limitó añadiendo condiciones. A es otro significado de "qualified" que aquí no encaja; C es demasiado fuerte, porque la idea central se mantuvo.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that members of a tightly knit circle "tend to know the same people"?
options: To argue that close friends are usually unwilling to help
To explain why close contacts often provide little new information
To show that the study included too few professional workers
To describe how acquaintances eventually become close friends

why.en: Author's purpose: it is part of the structural explanation, in which close friends share the same information while acquaintances bring news from other circles. A contradicts "more willing to offer assistance".
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: bu, yapısal açıklamanın parçası; yakın arkadaşlar aynı bilgiyi paylaşırken tanıdıklar başka çevrelerden haber getirir. A "more willing to offer assistance" bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Propósito del autor: forma parte de la explicación estructural: los amigos íntimos comparten la misma información, mientras que los conocidos traen noticias de otros círculos. A contradice "more willing to offer assistance".

questions.stem: Based on the passage, in which situation would a strong tie most likely be more useful than a weak one?
options: When news about job openings is easy to find
When a person wants news from unfamiliar social circles
When an employer wants a reliable personal reference
When acquaintances belong to many different groups

why.en: Inference: strong ties matter more "when a recommendation requires considerable trust". A is the opposite of "information is scarce"; B and D describe situations in which weak ties are the useful ones.
why.tr: Çıkarım: güçlü bağlar "when a recommendation requires considerable trust" durumunda daha etkili. A "information is scarce" ifadesinin tersi; B ve D zayıf bağların işe yaradığı durumları anlatıyor.
why.es: Inferencia: los lazos fuertes pesan más "when a recommendation requires considerable trust". A es lo contrario de "information is scarce"; B y D describen situaciones en las que son útiles los lazos débiles.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what did the study of professional workers find?
options: Job news came more often from acquaintances than from friends
Close friends were the most common source of job leads
Most workers found their jobs without help from any personal contacts
Acquaintances gave less reliable information than friends

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): people more often heard about the position "from acquaintances than from close friends". B reverses the finding; C contradicts "obtained jobs through personal contacts".
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): insanlar iş ilanını daha çok "from acquaintances than from close friends" duymuştu. B bulguyu tersine çeviriyor; C "obtained jobs through personal contacts" bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): la gente se enteraba del puesto más a menudo "from acquaintances than from close friends". B invierte el hallazgo; C contradice "obtained jobs through personal contacts".

screen.title: Why Crickets Chirp
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — lower module
text: On summer evenings, the sound of crickets fills many fields and gardens. Only male crickets make this sound. A male rubs the edge of one wing against a row of small ridges on the other wing, a little like running a fingernail along a comb.

Most chirping is meant to attract females, which hear the sound through tiny openings on their front legs. Males also use a different song to warn other males to stay away. Crickets chirp faster when the air is warm and more slowly when it is cool, so some people use them to estimate the temperature.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How and why crickets make their sound
Why crickets are found mainly in fields and gardens
How female crickets choose which male to follow
Why crickets are quieter on warm summer nights

why.en: Main idea: the passage explains how the sound is made and what it is used for. D contradicts the text, because crickets chirp faster when it is warm. C is never discussed.
why.tr: Ana fikir: metin sesin nasıl çıkarıldığını ve ne işe yaradığını anlatıyor. D metinle çelişiyor, çünkü cırcır böcekleri havada sıcakken daha hızlı öter. C metinde hiç ele alınmıyor.
why.es: Idea principal: el texto explica cómo se produce el sonido y para qué sirve. D contradice el texto, porque los grillos cantan más rápido cuando hace calor. C no se trata en ningún momento.

questions.stem: According to the passage, how does a male cricket make its sound?
options: By opening and closing its mouth quickly
By rubbing one wing against the other
By tapping its front legs on the ground
By pushing air through openings on its legs

why.en: Detail: a male "rubs the edge of one wing against" ridges on the other wing. D is the trap: the openings on the legs are how females hear, not how males make sound.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: erkek böcek "rubs the edge of one wing against" diğer kanattaki çıkıntılara. D tuzak: bacaklardaki açıklıklar dişilerin duymasını sağlar, erkeklerin ses çıkarmasını değil.
why.es: Detalle: el macho "rubs the edge of one wing against" las crestas de la otra ala. D es la trampa: las aberturas de las patas sirven para que las hembras oigan, no para que los machos produzcan el sonido.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention "a fingernail along a comb"?
options: To show that crickets have very sharp edges on their legs
To explain why some people find the sound unpleasant
To compare the cricket's song with human music
To help readers picture how the sound is made

why.en: Author's purpose: a familiar comparison that helps the reader imagine the movement. B is the trap: the comparison describes how the sound is produced, not whether it is pleasant. A moves the ridges from the wings to the legs.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: okurun hareketi gözünde canlandırmasına yardım eden tanıdık bir karşılaştırma. B tuzak: karşılaştırma sesin nasıl çıktığını anlatıyor, hoş olup olmadığını değil. A çıkıntıları kanatlardan bacaklara taşıyor.
why.es: Propósito del autor: una comparación conocida que ayuda al lector a imaginar el movimiento. B es la trampa: la comparación describe cómo se produce el sonido, no si es agradable. A traslada las crestas de las alas a las patas.

questions.stem: The word "estimate" in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: change on purpose
pay no attention to
roughly judge
carefully record

why.en: Vocabulary in context: people use crickets to estimate, that is, roughly judge, the temperature. D is too exact; crickets give only an approximate idea of the temperature.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: insanlar cırcır böceklerini sıcaklığı "estimate" etmek, yani kabaca tahmin etmek için kullanıyor. D fazla kesin; böcekler sıcaklık hakkında yalnızca yaklaşık bir fikir verir.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: la gente usa los grillos para "estimate", es decir, calcular aproximadamente, la temperatura. D es demasiado exacta; los grillos solo dan una idea aproximada de la temperatura.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about crickets on a cold evening?
options: Only the females will make any sound
Their chirps will come more slowly
They will switch to their warning song
They will fly to warmer fields to sing

why.en: Inference: crickets chirp "more slowly when it is cool", so on a cold evening the chirps come at a slower rate. A contradicts the fact that only males make the sound. C and D are not supported by the passage.
why.tr: Çıkarım: cırcır böcekleri "more slowly when it is cool" öter; dolayısıyla soğuk bir akşamda ötüşler daha yavaş gelir. A yalnızca erkeklerin ses çıkardığı bilgisiyle çelişiyor. C ve D metinle desteklenmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: los grillos cantan "more slowly when it is cool", así que en una tarde fría el canto será más lento. A contradice que solo los machos producen el sonido. C y D no tienen apoyo en el texto.

screen.title: The First Coins
text: For thousands of years, people traded using pieces of metal, such as silver, whose value depended on their weight and purity. Every sale therefore required a scale, and buyers often cut bits from a larger piece to pay the exact amount. Sellers also had to worry that the metal had been mixed with cheaper materials.

More than 2,600 years ago, rulers in Lydia, a kingdom in what is now western Turkey, began producing small lumps of metal of a standard weight and stamping each one with an official image. The stamp acted as a guarantee: people no longer needed to weigh or test every piece, because the state stood behind its value.

The idea spread quickly to Greek cities, which created their own designs. Before long, coins were used not only in markets but also to pay soldiers and collect taxes, which made it far easier for governments to manage large economies.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why silver was more valuable than other metals in ancient trade
How Greek cities competed with Lydia for control of markets
How an official mark on metal made buying and selling simpler
Why ancient governments found it difficult to collect taxes

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): stamped pieces of a standard weight removed the need to weigh and test metal. B invents a rivalry that the passage never mentions. D reverses the point; coins made taxes easier to collect.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): standart ağırlıkta ve damgalı metal parçaları, metali tartma ve test etme ihtiyacını ortadan kaldırdı. B metinde hiç geçmeyen bir rekabet uyduruyor. D fikri tersine çeviriyor; madeni paralar vergi toplamayı kolaylaştırdı.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): las piezas selladas de peso estándar eliminaron la necesidad de pesar y comprobar el metal. B inventa una rivalidad que el texto nunca menciona. D invierte la idea; las monedas facilitaron el cobro de impuestos.

questions.stem: The word "guarantee" in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: an assurance
a decoration
a payment
a warning

why.en: Vocabulary in context: the stamp was a guarantee because the state "stood behind" the value of each piece, so it was an assurance. B describes what the image looks like, not what it does.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: damga bir "guarantee" idi, çünkü devlet her parçanın değerinin arkasında duruyordu ("stood behind"); yani bir güvenceydi. B resmin neye benzediğini anlatıyor, ne işe yaradığını değil.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: el sello era una garantía porque el Estado "stood behind" el valor de cada pieza; es decir, era una seguridad. B describe el aspecto de la imagen, no su función.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that buyers "cut bits from a larger piece"?
options: To show that early metal was softer than modern coins
To explain how merchants made their own coins
To suggest that buyers often tried to cheat sellers
To illustrate how awkward payment was before coins

why.en: Author's purpose: cutting metal to the right amount is an example of the inconvenience that coins later removed. C confuses this with the separate worry about mixed metal. B is wrong because coins did not exist yet at that point.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: metali doğru miktarda kesmek, madeni paraların daha sonra ortadan kaldırdığı zahmete bir örnek. C bunu ayrı bir endişe olan karışık metal meselesiyle karıştırıyor. B yanlış, çünkü o dönemde henüz madeni para yoktu.
why.es: Propósito del autor: cortar el metal en la cantidad justa es un ejemplo de la incomodidad que las monedas eliminaron después. C lo confunde con la preocupación distinta del metal mezclado. B es incorrecta porque en ese momento aún no existían las monedas.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about trade before coins were invented?
options: Most buyers preferred to pay with goods rather than with metal
A seller could receive metal worth less than it seemed to be
Only government officials were allowed to own a scale
Silver was used only for very large purchases

why.en: Inference: sellers worried that the metal "had been mixed with cheaper materials", so a payment could be worth less than it looked. A is never mentioned. D contradicts the statement that every sale required a scale.
why.tr: Çıkarım: satıcılar metalin "had been mixed with cheaper materials" olmasından endişe ediyordu; yani bir ödeme göründüğünden daha az değerli olabiliyordu. A metinde hiç geçmiyor. D, her satışın bir terazi gerektirdiği bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: a los vendedores les preocupaba que el metal "had been mixed with cheaper materials", así que un pago podía valer menos de lo que parecía. A no se menciona nunca. D contradice que cada venta necesitaba una balanza.

questions.stem: According to the passage, coins were later used for which of the following?
options: Measuring the purity of other metals
Decorating buildings in Greek cities
Paying soldiers for their service
Weighing goods at the market

why.en: Detail: coins were used "to pay soldiers and collect taxes". B twists "created their own designs". D confuses coins with the scales they replaced.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: madeni paralar "to pay soldiers and collect taxes" için kullanıldı. B "created their own designs" ifadesini çarpıtıyor. D madeni paraları, yerini aldıkları terazilerle karıştırıyor.
why.es: Detalle: las monedas se usaron "to pay soldiers and collect taxes". B tergiversa "created their own designs". D confunde las monedas con las balanzas que sustituyeron.

screen.title: What Infants Expect
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — upper module
text: For much of the twentieth century, the dominant account of infant cognition held that babies younger than about eight months lack object permanence, the understanding that objects continue to exist when they are out of sight. This conclusion rested largely on search tasks: when an attractive toy was covered by a cloth, young infants typically made no attempt to retrieve it.

Beginning in the 1980s, however, researchers adopted an alternative method that did not depend on reaching. Exploiting infants' tendency to look longer at surprising events, they presented apparently impossible scenes, such as a screen rotating straight through the space occupied by a hidden box. Infants as young as four months stared reliably longer at these outcomes, suggesting that they mentally represented the concealed object.

Critics caution that prolonged looking may reflect perceptual novelty rather than genuine reasoning about objects. Even so, the findings have persuaded many developmental psychologists that earlier failures revealed limitations in planning and coordinating actions rather than an absence of knowledge.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why infants prefer attractive toys to the ordinary objects around them
How a different method changed views of what babies understand
Why critics reject every study that measures how long infants look
How infants gradually learn to coordinate their reaching and looking

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): looking-time studies suggested that infants know more than search tasks had shown. C is too extreme; critics raise a doubt, but they do not reject every study. D turns a detail from the last sentence into the topic.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): bakış süresi çalışmaları bebeklerin, arama görevlerinin gösterdiğinden daha fazlasını bildiğini düşündürdü. C aşırı; eleştirmenler bir şüphe dile getiriyor ama her çalışmayı reddetmiyor. D son cümledeki bir ayrıntıyı konunun kendisi yapıyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): los estudios de tiempo de mirada sugirieron que los bebés saben más de lo que mostraban las tareas de búsqueda. C es demasiado extremo; los críticos plantean una duda, pero no rechazan todos los estudios. D convierte un detalle de la última frase en el tema.

questions.stem: The word "Exploiting" in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: Paying no attention to
Measuring precisely
Calling into question
Making use of

why.en: Vocabulary in context: researchers exploited, that is, made use of, infants' habit of looking longer at surprising events. B is tempting because looking time was measured, but the verb refers to taking advantage of the habit.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: araştırmacılar bebeklerin şaşırtıcı olaylara daha uzun bakma eğiliminden yararlandı ("exploiting" = making use of). B çekici görünüyor çünkü bakış süresi ölçüldü; ama fiil bu eğilimden faydalanmayı anlatıyor.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: los investigadores aprovecharon ("exploiting" = making use of) la tendencia de los bebés a mirar más tiempo los sucesos sorprendentes. B resulta tentadora porque se midió el tiempo de mirada, pero el verbo se refiere a aprovechar esa tendencia.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention "a screen rotating straight through the space occupied by a hidden box"?
options: To illustrate an event that should surprise an infant aware of the box
To show how researchers taught infants to reach for objects behind screens
To describe a toy that infants found more attractive than a cloth
To explain why earlier search tasks produced unreliable results

why.en: Author's purpose: the impossible scene is an example of an event that only surprises an infant who represents the hidden box. B is wrong because the new method "did not depend on reaching". D is not the reason the example is given.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: bu imkânsız sahne, yalnızca gizli kutuyu zihninde canlandıran bir bebeği şaşırtacak bir olaya örnek. B yanlış, çünkü yeni yöntem "did not depend on reaching". D örneğin veriliş amacı değil.
why.es: Propósito del autor: la escena imposible es un ejemplo de un suceso que solo sorprende a un bebé que se representa la caja escondida. B es incorrecta porque el nuevo método "did not depend on reaching". D no es la razón por la que se da el ejemplo.

questions.stem: What does the author suggest about infants who did not search for a covered toy?
options: They had not yet noticed that the toy was attractive
They were still too young to see any object partly hidden by a cloth
They may have known it was there but been unable to act on it
They were probably reacting to the novelty of the cloth

why.en: Inference: the last sentence says earlier failures reflected limits in "planning and coordinating actions" rather than missing knowledge. D applies the critics' novelty argument to the wrong studies. B is never claimed in the passage.
why.tr: Çıkarım: son cümle, önceki başarısızlıkların bilgi eksikliğinden değil "planning and coordinating actions" konusundaki sınırlılıklardan kaynaklandığını söylüyor. D eleştirmenlerin yenilik argümanını yanlış çalışmalara uyguluyor. B metinde hiç iddia edilmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: la última frase dice que los fallos anteriores reflejaban límites en "planning and coordinating actions" y no falta de conocimiento. D aplica el argumento de la novedad de los críticos a los estudios equivocados. B no se afirma en el texto.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what concern do critics raise about the newer studies?
options: The studies tested too few infants to be reliable
Four-month-olds cannot see a rotating screen clearly
The scenes were not truly impossible in the real world
Infants might look longer simply because a scene is new to them

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): longer looking "may reflect perceptual novelty", meaning the scene is simply new to the infant. A sounds like a typical criticism, but the passage never mentions how many infants were tested.
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): daha uzun bakmak "may reflect perceptual novelty"; yani sahne bebek için sadece yeni olabilir. A tipik bir eleştiri gibi duruyor ama metin kaç bebeğin test edildiğinden hiç söz etmiyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): mirar más tiempo "may reflect perceptual novelty", es decir, la escena simplemente es nueva para el bebé. A parece una crítica típica, pero el texto nunca menciona cuántos bebés participaron.

screen.title: Flowers That Open at Night
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — lower module
text: Most flowers open during the day, when bees and butterflies are busy. Some plants, however, open their flowers only at night. These plants depend on night animals, such as moths and bats, to carry their pollen from flower to flower.

Night flowers are often white or pale, so they are easy to see in moonlight. Many also have a strong, sweet smell that moths can follow from far away. Flowers visited by bats are usually large and strong, because bats are heavy and push their heads deep inside to drink.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why bees and butterflies stop working at night
How some flowers are suited to animals that visit at night
Why moths are more useful to plants than bats are
How gardeners can grow flowers that bloom only in the moonlight

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): the passage describes how night flowers match moths and bats. A misreads the first sentence; C and D are never discussed.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): metin gece açan çiçeklerin güvelere ve yarasalara nasıl uyduğunu anlatıyor. A ilk cümleyi yanlış okuyor; C ve D hiç ele alınmıyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): el texto describe cómo las flores nocturnas se adaptan a las polillas y los murciélagos. A malinterpreta la primera frase; C y D no se tratan.

questions.stem: The word "pale" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: light in color
very small
easy to break
sweet-smelling

why.en: Vocabulary in context: "white or pale" flowers are "easy to see in moonlight", so pale means light in color. D describes the smell mentioned in the next sentence.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: "white or pale" çiçekler "ay ışığında kolay görülüyor"; pale açık renkli demek. D bir sonraki cümledeki kokuyu anlatıyor.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: las flores "white or pale" son "fáciles de ver a la luz de la luna", así que pale significa de color claro. D describe el olor de la frase siguiente.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that bats are heavy?
options: To explain why some night flowers are large and strong
To show that bats are dangerous to small plants
To compare the size of bats with the much smaller size of moths
To explain why bats cannot see in the moonlight

why.en: Author's purpose: the bats' weight explains why the flowers they visit are "large and strong". B and D are not stated; C is not the point being made.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: yarasaların ağırlığı, ziyaret ettikleri çiçeklerin neden "large and strong" olduğunu açıklıyor. B ve D metinde yok; C anlatılmak istenen nokta değil.
why.es: Propósito del autor: el peso de los murciélagos explica por qué las flores que visitan son "large and strong". B y D no se dicen; C no es la idea que se quiere mostrar.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about moths?
options: They are active mainly during the day
They prefer brightly colored flowers
They are too heavy to land on most flowers
They find some flowers by their smell

why.en: Inference from "a strong, sweet smell that moths can follow from far away". A contradicts "night animals"; C describes bats; B contradicts "white or pale".
why.tr: "A strong, sweet smell that moths can follow from far away" ifadesinden çıkarım. A "night animals" ile çelişiyor; C yarasaları anlatıyor; B "white or pale" ile çelişiyor.
why.es: Inferencia a partir de "a strong, sweet smell that moths can follow from far away". A contradice "night animals"; C describe a los murciélagos; B contradice "white or pale".

questions.stem: According to the passage, why do bats push their heads deep into flowers?
options: To hide from other animals
To drink from the flower
To keep the flower closed
To clean the flower

why.en: Detail: bats "push their heads deep inside to drink". A, C and D give reasons the passage never mentions.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: yarasalar "push their heads deep inside to drink". A, C ve D metinde geçmeyen gerekçeler veriyor.
why.es: Detalle: los murciélagos "push their heads deep inside to drink". A, C y D dan razones que el texto no menciona.

screen.title: How Printing Changed Spelling
text: Before the printing press reached England in the late fifteenth century, English spelling varied widely. Writers spelled words as they heard them, and the same scribe might write a common word in two or three ways on a single page.

Printing gradually reduced this variety. Because a printer produced hundreds of identical copies, readers across the country began to see the same forms again and again. Printers also had practical reasons to settle on fixed spellings, since consistent forms made it faster to set the metal type for each page.

The change was slow, however. Early printers sometimes added or removed letters simply to fill a line evenly, and many spellings did not become stable until dictionaries appeared in the eighteenth century. Even so, historians generally agree that printing started the movement toward standard spelling.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why scribes preferred writing by hand to using the printing press
How a machine for copying text made written words more alike
Why eighteenth-century dictionaries contained many spelling mistakes
How printers set metal type to produce identical pages quickly

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase of "printing started the movement toward standard spelling"). D is only one supporting detail; C is not stated; A invents a preference.
why.tr: Ana fikir ("printing started the movement toward standard spelling" ifadesinin parafrazı). D yalnızca destekleyici bir ayrıntı; C metinde yok; A bir tercih uyduruyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis de "printing started the movement toward standard spelling"). D es solo un detalle de apoyo; C no se dice; A inventa una preferencia.

questions.stem: The word "settle on" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: argue about
decide on
look for
write down

why.en: Vocabulary in context: printers wanted to "settle on fixed spellings", that is, choose them and keep them. A is close to the opposite; C and D do not fit "fixed spellings".
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: matbaacılar "settle on fixed spellings" istiyordu, yani yazımları seçip korumak. A neredeyse tersi; C ve D "fixed spellings" ile uyuşmuyor.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: los impresores querían "settle on fixed spellings", es decir, elegirlas y mantenerlas. A es casi lo contrario; C y D no encajan con "fixed spellings".

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that printers added or removed letters to fill a line?
options: To show that printing did not make spelling consistent right away
To explain why printed books were usually cheaper than handwritten ones
To suggest that printers did not know how to spell correctly
To prove that dictionaries were based on early printed books

why.en: Author's purpose: the example supports "The change was slow". C reads too much into it: the letters changed for layout, not from ignorance. B and D are never discussed.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: örnek "The change was slow" ifadesini destekliyor. C fazla yorum katıyor: harfler bilgisizlikten değil sayfa düzeni için değişiyordu. B ve D hiç ele alınmıyor.
why.es: Propósito del autor: el ejemplo apoya "The change was slow". C interpreta de más: las letras cambiaban por la maquetación, no por ignorancia. B y D no se tratan.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about spelling before the printing press?
options: Most writers followed the rules of an early English dictionary
Spelling depended more on how words sounded to each writer
Only scribes in large cities were allowed to write official documents
Readers found handwritten texts easier to understand than printed ones

why.en: Inference from "Writers spelled words as they heard them". A contradicts the timeline: dictionaries came much later. C and D are not supported.
why.tr: "Writers spelled words as they heard them" ifadesinden çıkarım. A zaman sırasıyla çelişiyor: sözlükler çok sonra geldi. C ve D metinle desteklenmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia a partir de "Writers spelled words as they heard them". A contradice la cronología: los diccionarios llegaron mucho después. C y D no tienen apoyo.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, why did printers prefer consistent spellings?
options: Readers complained when words appeared in unfamiliar forms
The government required printers to use official spellings
It saved time when they were getting pages ready
Scribes refused to work with printers who changed spellings

why.en: Detail (paraphrase of "consistent forms made it faster to set the metal type"). A, B and D give reasons the passage never mentions.
why.tr: Ayrıntı ("consistent forms made it faster to set the metal type" ifadesinin parafrazı). A, B ve D metinde hiç geçmeyen gerekçeler veriyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "consistent forms made it faster to set the metal type"). A, B y D dan razones que el texto nunca menciona.

screen.title: Why Wages Rarely Fall
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — upper module
text: Elementary economic theory predicts that when the demand for labor declines, wages should fall until employers are again willing to hire everyone seeking work. Empirical studies, however, consistently find that nominal wages are remarkably resistant to reduction, even during severe recessions; firms typically respond to weaker demand by dismissing employees rather than by lowering pay.

Economists have proposed several explanations for this rigidity. screen.title: Revised Overnight Parking Policy

Commuter permits will remain valid in these lots between 7 a.m. and 10 p.m. only; vehicles without a resident permit that remain after 10 p.m. may be towed at the owner's expense. Lot E, behind the stadium, will continue to allow overnight parking for all permit holders.

Overnight parking in two lots will be reserved for residents
Lot E will now close to all vehicles at 10 p.m.
Resident permits will be given out free of charge

why.en: Main change (paraphrase). A is too extreme (commuters can still park there during the day); C contradicts the last sentence.
why.tr: Ana değişiklik (parafraz). A aşırı genelleme (gündüz hâlâ park edebilirler); C son cümleyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Cambio principal (paráfrasis). A es demasiado extremo (los que vienen en coche pueden seguir aparcando allí de día); C contradice la última frase.

Request a pass from Campus Security on the night itself
Ask Campus Security for a pass at least a day earlier
Park in Lot C and move the car before 7 a.m.

why.tr: Çıkarım: geçiş izni 24 saat önceden istenmeli. B zamanlama tuzağı; D yolcu izinleri için 22.00 sınırını yok sayıyor.
why.es: Inferencia: los pases deben pedirse con 24 horas de antelación. B es la trampa de la hora; D ignora el límite de las 10 p. m. para los permisos de commuter.

why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "continue to allow overnight parking for all permit holders"). A y B aplican las nuevas normas de los aparcamientos C/D al aparcamiento equivocado.

They expire at the end of each term

screen.title: Building email: water shut-off
text:
From: Daniel Reyes (Apartment 4B)
To: All residents
Subject: Water shut-off on Thursday

Hi everyone, the building manager asked me to pass this on. Workers will replace the main water pipe on Thursday, so the water will be turned off from 9 a.m. to about 3 p.m. Please fill a few bottles the night before if you need water for cooking. The laundry room will also be closed that day, but it will reopen on Friday morning with two new washing machines. If you have questions, please contact the office directly rather than replying to this email.
— Daniel

questions.stem: Why did Daniel write the email?
options: To ask the manager to repair a pipe in his apartment
To invite residents to try the new washing machines
To warn neighbors about a planned interruption in service
To complain about the noise from the construction work next door

why.en: Purpose (paraphrase): the water will be turned off for repairs. A misreads who is asking for the repair; B picks a minor detail.
why.tr: Amaç (parafraz): onarım için suyun kesileceği uyarısı. A onarımı kimin istediğini yanlış okuyor; B küçük bir ayrıntıyı ana amaç sanıyor.
why.es: Propósito (paráfrasis): se cortará el agua por unas reparaciones. A malinterpreta quién pide la reparación; B se queda con un detalle menor.

questions.stem: What are residents advised to do?
options: Do their laundry early on Thursday morning
Send any questions to Daniel by email
Avoid cooking until the pipe is replaced
Store some water before the work begins

why.en: Paraphrase of "fill a few bottles the night before". B contradicts the email (contact the office, not Daniel); A is impossible because the laundry room is closed.
why.tr: "Fill a few bottles the night before" ifadesinin parafrazı. B e-postayla çelişiyor (Daniel'e değil ofise yazılmalı); A imkânsız çünkü çamaşırhane kapalı.
why.es: Paráfrasis de "fill a few bottles the night before". B contradice el correo (hay que contactar con la oficina, no con Daniel); A es imposible porque la lavandería está cerrada.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the laundry room?
options: It will be closed for the rest of the week
Its equipment is being upgraded
It is the reason the water must be turned off
It will be open only to residents of Apartment 4B

why.en: Inference: it "will reopen ... with two new washing machines". A contradicts "reopen on Friday"; C confuses the cause of the shut-off.
why.tr: Çıkarım: "iki yeni çamaşır makinesiyle yeniden açılacak". A "Cuma açılacak" bilgisiyle çelişiyor; C kesintinin nedenini karıştırıyor.
why.es: Inferencia: "will reopen ... with two new washing machines". A contradice "reopen on Friday"; C confunde la causa del corte.

screen.title: Updated Course Withdrawal Policy
text: Updated Course Withdrawal Policy

Beginning this fall, students may withdraw from a course through the student portal until the end of the tenth week of the semester; previously, the limit was the eighth week. Withdrawals made after the second week will appear on the transcript as a "W," which does not affect the grade point average. Tuition is refunded in full only for withdrawals completed during the first two weeks. Students holding scholarships that require full-time enrollment should consult the Financial Aid Office before withdrawing, since dropping below twelve credits may reduce their award. After the tenth week, withdrawals are approved only in documented exceptional circumstances.

questions.stem: What is the main change described in the notice?
options: Students can no longer withdraw through the online portal
Tuition refunds will now cover the first ten weeks of a term
A "W" on the transcript will now lower the grade point average
The period for leaving a class has been extended

why.en: Main change (paraphrase): the deadline moves from the eighth to the tenth week. B mixes up the refund period with the withdrawal deadline; C contradicts "does not affect the grade point average".
why.tr: Ana değişiklik (parafraz): son tarih sekizinci haftadan onuncu haftaya kayıyor. B ücret iadesi süresini çekilme son tarihiyle karıştırıyor; C "does not affect the grade point average" bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Cambio principal (paráfrasis): el plazo pasa de la octava a la décima semana. B confunde el periodo de reembolso con el plazo para retirarse; C contradice "does not affect the grade point average".

questions.stem: What can be inferred about a student who withdraws from a course in the fourth week?
options: The course will not appear on the student's transcript
Not all of the money they paid will be returned
The student's grade point average will be lowered
The student must provide documents explaining the decision

why.en: Inference: full refunds are given only in the first two weeks, so a fourth-week withdrawal does not qualify. A applies only to very early withdrawals (a "W" appears after week two); D describes withdrawals after the tenth week.
why.tr: Çıkarım: tam iade yalnızca ilk iki haftada yapılıyor, dördüncü haftadaki çekilme bu kapsama girmiyor. A yalnızca çok erken çekilmeler için geçerli (ikinci haftadan sonra transkriptte "W" görünür); D onuncu haftadan sonraki çekilmeleri anlatıyor.
why.es: Inferencia: el reembolso completo solo se da en las dos primeras semanas, así que retirarse en la cuarta no da derecho a él. A solo vale para retiradas muy tempranas (tras la segunda semana aparece una "W"); D describe las retiradas después de la décima semana.

questions.stem: Why should some scholarship holders contact the Financial Aid Office?
options: Their scholarships pay tuition only for the first two weeks
They are not allowed to use the student portal to withdraw
Taking fewer credits could reduce the money they receive
They need special approval to take more than twelve credits

why.en: Detail (paraphrase of "dropping below twelve credits may reduce their award"). D reverses the direction (more instead of fewer credits); A borrows the two-week refund rule.
why.tr: Ayrıntı ("dropping below twelve credits may reduce their award" ifadesinin parafrazı). D yönü tersine çeviriyor (daha az yerine daha fazla kredi); A iki haftalık iade kuralını ödünç alıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "dropping below twelve credits may reduce their award"). D invierte la dirección (más créditos en vez de menos); A toma prestada la regla del reembolso de dos semanas.

screen.title: Notice: Graduation Photo Day
text: Graduation Photo Day — Thursday, April 17

Graduating students can have their official portraits taken free of charge in the Student Union ballroom between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m. Gowns will be provided, but please bring your own tie or scarf if you would like to wear one. To keep waiting times short, choose a fifteen-minute time slot on the alumni website by Monday. Students who arrive without a booking will be photographed only if a slot becomes free.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To announce that the graduation ceremony will be held in the ballroom
To explain how final-year students can get their official photos
To ask graduating students to return the gowns they borrowed
To advertise a photography course for students in their last year

why.en: Main purpose (paraphrase): the notice tells graduating students how to have their portraits taken. A confuses the photo session with the ceremony; C misuses the word "gowns", which will be provided on the day.
why.tr: Ana amaç (parafraz): duyuru, mezun olacak öğrencilere portre fotoğraflarını nasıl çektireceklerini anlatıyor. A fotoğraf çekimini mezuniyet töreniyle karıştırıyor; C "gowns" kelimesini yanlış kullanıyor, cübbeler o gün zaten verilecek.
why.es: Propósito principal (paráfrasis): el aviso explica a quienes se gradúan cómo hacerse el retrato oficial. A confunde la sesión de fotos con la ceremonia; C usa mal la palabra "gowns": las togas se entregan ese mismo día.

questions.stem: What are students asked to do by Monday?
options: Pay a small fee for their portrait at the union
Collect a gown from the Student Union ballroom
Bring a tie or scarf to the alumni office
Reserve a time on the alumni website

why.en: Detail (paraphrase of "choose a fifteen-minute time slot ... by Monday"). A contradicts "free of charge"; B misreads the gown information, since gowns are handed out at the session itself.
why.tr: Ayrıntı ("choose a fifteen-minute time slot ... by Monday" ifadesinin parafrazı). A "free of charge" bilgisiyle çelişiyor; B cübbe bilgisini yanlış okuyor, cübbeler çekimin kendisinde veriliyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "choose a fifteen-minute time slot ... by Monday"). A contradice "free of charge"; B malinterpreta lo de las togas, que se entregan en la propia sesión.

screen.title: Lab email: booking the microscopes
text:
From: Lena Hoffmann, Biology Lab Coordinator
To: Biology 210 students
Subject: Booking the microscopes

Hi all, starting next week, the four digital microscopes in Room 118 must be booked through the department's online calendar instead of the paper sign-up sheet. Each booking can last up to two hours, and you may hold only one future booking at a time. If you can't use your slot, please cancel it at least a day ahead so that classmates can take it. Students who miss two bookings without cancelling will lose access for the rest of the month.
— Lena

questions.stem: Why did Lena write the email?
options: To announce that the microscopes in Room 118 will be replaced
To ask students to write their names on the paper sign-up sheet
To describe a new procedure for reserving equipment
To remind students that their lab reports are due next week

why.en: Purpose (paraphrase): the email explains the new online booking rules. B describes the old method that is being replaced; A wrongly assumes the microscopes themselves are changing.
why.tr: Amaç (parafraz): e-posta yeni çevrim içi rezervasyon kurallarını açıklıyor. B kaldırılan eski yöntemi anlatıyor; A mikroskopların değiştirileceğini sanıyor.
why.es: Propósito (paráfrasis): el correo explica las nuevas normas de reserva en línea. B describe el método antiguo que se elimina; A supone por error que se cambian los microscopios.

questions.stem: What should a student do if they cannot use a booked slot?
options: Cancel it at least one day in advance
Give the slot to a classmate
Email Lena before the session begins
Book a second slot later in the week

why.en: Detail (close to "cancel it at least a day ahead"). B misreads "so that classmates can take it": the slot is freed by cancelling, not handed over; D breaks the one-booking rule.
why.tr: Ayrıntı ("cancel it at least a day ahead" ifadesine yakın). B "so that classmates can take it" kısmını yanlış okuyor: saat iptal edilerek boşaltılır, birine devredilmez; D tek rezervasyon kuralını çiğniyor.
why.es: Detalle (cercano a "cancel it at least a day ahead"). B malinterpreta "so that classmates can take it": el turno se libera cancelándolo, no se cede; D incumple la regla de una sola reserva.

questions.stem: What is true about the new booking rules?
options: Bookings longer than two hours need special permission
Students who cancel twice will lose access for a month
The paper sign-up sheet can still be used in emergencies
A student cannot reserve several future sessions at once

why.en: Detail from "you may hold only one future booking at a time". B changes the rule: access is lost for missing bookings without cancelling, not for cancelling; A adds a permission that is never mentioned.
why.tr: "You may hold only one future booking at a time" ifadesinden çıkarım. B kuralı değiştiriyor: erişim, iptal etmeden gelmemek yüzünden kaybedilir, iptal etmek yüzünden değil; A hiç söz edilmeyen bir izin ekliyor.
why.es: Detalle a partir de "you may hold only one future booking at a time". B cambia la norma: el acceso se pierde por faltar sin cancelar, no por cancelar; A añade un permiso que nunca se menciona.

screen.title: Replacing a Student ID
text: Lost Your Student ID Card?

New cards are made at the Card Office, Room 110, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Please bring a photo ID, such as a passport. A new card costs $15. If your card was stolen, show a police report and the new card is free.

questions.stem: When can students get a new card?
options: Any day of the week, all day
On Saturday and Sunday mornings
From Monday to Friday
Every evening after 4 p.m.

why.en: Detail: the Card Office is open "Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m." B names the weekend, when the office is closed. D gives a time after the office closes.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: kart ofisi "Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m." açık. B ofisin kapalı olduğu hafta sonunu söylüyor. D ofis kapandıktan sonraki bir saati veriyor.
why.es: Detalle: la oficina abre "Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m." B menciona el fin de semana, cuando la oficina está cerrada. D da una hora en la que la oficina ya ha cerrado.

why.tr: Ayrıntı: "If your card was stolen, show a police report and the new card is free." B tuzak: fotoğraflı kimliği herkes getirmeli ve bu kartı ücretsiz yapmıyor. C "report" kelimesini farklı bir anlamda kullanıyor.
why.es: Detalle: "If your card was stolen, show a police report and the new card is free." B es la trampa: todos deben llevar un documento con foto y eso no hace gratuita la tarjeta. C reutiliza "report" con otro significado.

screen.title: Class email: museum visit
text:
From: Professor Lena Brandt
To: HIST 215 students

Hi all, a few reminders about Friday's trip to the City History Museum. The bus leaves from Hollis Hall at 9:15, and the driver cannot wait for latecomers. questions.stem: Why did Professor Brandt send the email?

To ask students to pay for their museum tickets in advance
To remind students that their response papers are due Monday
To explain why backpacks are not allowed inside the museum galleries

why.en: Purpose: the email reminds students of the arrangements for Friday's trip. B contradicts "The department is paying for admission". C gives the old deadline; the paper is now due Wednesday.

why.es: Propósito: el correo recuerda a los estudiantes los detalles de la salida del viernes. B contradice "The department is paying for admission". C da la fecha antigua; el trabajo ahora se entrega el miércoles.

questions.stem: Why are students told to bring a pencil?
options: Pencils are cheaper than pens at the museum shop
Students will be asked to draw some of the paintings
Ink could damage some of the items on display
The bus driver does not allow pens on the bus

why.es: Inferencia: los bolígrafos "may not be used near the old documents", así que el museo protege su colección. B inventa una tarea de dibujo. D relaciona la norma con el autobús en lugar de con las salas.

questions.stem: What is true about the response paper?
options: It must be handed in at the museum on Friday
Students now have two more days to complete it
It will be written in small groups during the trip
It was postponed because the bus was running late
