why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): teslim tarihi pazartesiden çarşambaya, yani iki gün sonraya kaydı. D bir sebep uyduruyor; değişiklik öğrenciler daha fazla zaman istediği için yapıldı. A ödevi geziyle karıştırıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): la fecha pasó del lunes al miércoles, dos días más tarde. D inventa un motivo; el cambio se hizo porque los estudiantes pidieron más tiempo. A confunde el trabajo con la propia visita.

screen.title: Residence Life: New Recycling Rules
text: Residence Halls — New Recycling Rules

Beginning October 1, glass bottles and jars must go in the green bins in each building's basement instead of the blue bins on every floor. The blue bins will accept only paper, cans, and clean plastic containers. Pizza boxes and anything else with food on it belong in the regular trash. Halls that keep their bins correctly sorted all semester will be entered in a drawing for a free movie night.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To announce that the blue bins on each floor will be removed
To explain where residents should now put certain kinds of waste
To invite residents to help sort the recycling in the basement
To tell residents how they can sign up for a free movie night

why.en: Main purpose (paraphrase): the notice tells residents which bin to use for glass, for recyclables and for items with food on them. A is wrong because the blue bins stay; they simply accept fewer items. D turns a minor detail (the prize drawing) into the purpose.
why.tr: Ana amaç (parafraz): duyuru cam, geri dönüştürülebilir atıklar ve üzerinde yemek kalıntısı olan şeyler için hangi kutunun kullanılacağını anlatıyor. A yanlış, çünkü mavi kutular kaldırılmıyor; yalnızca daha az şey kabul ediyor. D küçük bir ayrıntıyı (ödül çekilişini) ana amaç sanıyor.
why.es: Propósito principal (paráfrasis): el aviso explica en qué contenedor va el vidrio, el material reciclable y lo que tiene restos de comida. A es incorrecta porque los contenedores azules se quedan; solo aceptan menos cosas. D convierte un detalle menor (el sorteo) en el propósito.

questions.stem: A resident has an empty yogurt container with some yogurt still inside. Where should it go?
options: Into one of the blue bins on that floor
Into a green bin in the basement
Next to the bins, for staff to sort later
In the regular trash

why.en: Application of a detail: the blue bins take only clean plastic, and anything with food on it belongs in the regular trash. A is the trap: the container is plastic, but it is not clean. B is only for glass bottles and jars.
why.tr: Ayrıntının uygulanması: mavi kutular yalnızca temiz plastik kabul ediyor; üzerinde yemek olan her şey normal çöpe gidiyor. A tuzak: kap plastik ama temiz değil. B yalnızca cam şişe ve kavanozlar için.
why.es: Aplicación de un detalle: los contenedores azules solo aceptan plástico limpio, y todo lo que tenga comida va a la basura normal. A es la trampa: el envase es de plástico, pero no está limpio. B es solo para botellas y frascos de vidrio.

screen.title: Fine Arts Studios: After-Hours Access
text: Fine Arts Studios — Revised After-Hours Access

Beginning next semester, students who wish to use the ceramics and printmaking studios after 6 p.m. must complete a one-hour safety session before their ID cards will be activated for evening entry. Sessions are held every Tuesday during the first four weeks of the term; students who completed the session last year need not repeat it. Only studio staff may load the kilns, and their shifts end at 8 p.m., so pieces to be fired should be placed on the labeled shelf before then. No one may work in the studios alone after 10 p.m. Daytime access remains unchanged.

questions.stem: What is the main change described in the notice?
options: The ceramics and printmaking studios will close to everyone at 6 p.m.
Students will need a new kind of ID card to enter the studios by day
Studio staff will now stay until 10 p.m. to help students with the kilns
Night-time access to two studios will depend on prior instruction

why.en: Main change (paraphrase): after 6 p.m. the two studios can be used only after a safety session. A is too extreme; the studios stay open in the evening for trained students. C contradicts the notice, since staff shifts end at 8 p.m.
why.tr: Ana değişiklik (parafraz): saat 18.00'den sonra iki atölye ancak güvenlik eğitiminden sonra kullanılabilecek. A aşırı; atölyeler eğitim almış öğrencilere akşam da açık. C duyuruyla çelişiyor, çünkü personelin mesaisi saat 20.00'de bitiyor.
why.es: Cambio principal (paráfrasis): después de las 6 p. m., los dos talleres solo se pueden usar tras una sesión de seguridad. A es demasiado extremo; los talleres siguen abiertos por la noche para quien tenga la formación. C contradice el aviso, porque el turno del personal termina a las 8 p. m.

questions.stem: A student wants a vase fired in a kiln. What should she do?
options: Leave the vase on the marked shelf before 8 p.m.
Load the kiln herself after the Tuesday session
Bring the vase to the studio after 10 p.m. with a friend
Ask a staff member to open the kiln room at 9 p.m.

why.en: Application: only staff may load the kilns, and they leave at 8 p.m., so the piece must be on the labeled shelf before then. B is the trap: the safety session does not allow students to load kilns. D asks for staff at an hour when they have already gone.
why.tr: Uygulama: fırınlara yalnızca personel yükleme yapabilir ve personel saat 20.00'de çıkıyor; bu yüzden eser ondan önce etiketli rafa konmalı. B tuzak: güvenlik eğitimi öğrencilere fırın yükleme izni vermiyor. D personelin çoktan gitmiş olduğu bir saatte yardım istiyor.
why.es: Aplicación: solo el personal puede cargar los hornos y se va a las 8 p. m., así que la pieza debe estar en el estante etiquetado antes de esa hora. B es la trampa: la sesión de seguridad no permite a los estudiantes cargar los hornos. D pide ayuda al personal a una hora en la que ya se ha ido.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about a student who attended the safety session last year?
options: She must attend another Tuesday session at the start of next term
She may stay in the studios alone at any hour of the night
She can get evening access without taking the session again
She is now permitted to load the kilns herself after 8 p.m.

why.en: Inference: students who "completed the session last year need not repeat it", so their cards can be activated without a new session. A contradicts this. B ignores the rule that no one may work alone after 10 p.m.
why.tr: Çıkarım: "completed the session last year need not repeat it" deniyor; yani bu öğrencinin kartı yeni bir eğitim almadan akşam girişine açılabilir. A bununla çelişiyor. B, saat 22.00'den sonra kimsenin yalnız çalışamayacağı kuralını yok sayıyor.
why.es: Inferencia: quienes "completed the session last year need not repeat it", así que su tarjeta se puede activar sin una nueva sesión. A contradice esto. B ignora la norma de que nadie puede trabajar solo después de las 10 p. m.

screen.title: Campus bike share
text: Campus Bike Share
Unlock a bike with your student ID at any station. The first 30 minutes are free. After that, each extra 30 minutes costs one dollar. Please return bikes to a station, not to a tree or a fence.

questions.stem: What do students need to take a bike?
options: A key from the station
Their student ID card
A one-dollar coin
A form from the office

why.en: Detail: "Unlock a bike with your student ID." C confuses the extra-time price with what you need to start; A and D are not mentioned.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: "Unlock a bike with your student ID." C ek süre ücretini başlamak için gereken şeyle karıştırıyor; A ve D hiç geçmiyor.
why.es: Detalle: "Unlock a bike with your student ID." C confunde el precio del tiempo extra con lo que se necesita para empezar; A y D no se mencionan.

questions.stem: How much does a one-hour ride cost?
options: Nothing
One dollar
Two dollars
Three dollars

why.en: Detail with a small calculation: the first 30 minutes are free and the next 30 minutes cost one dollar. A forgets the second half hour; C charges for the free part too.
why.tr: Küçük bir hesapla ayrıntı: ilk 30 dakika ücretsiz, sonraki 30 dakika bir dolar. A ikinci yarım saati unutuyor; C ücretsiz kısmı da ücretlendiriyor.
why.es: Detalle con un pequeño cálculo: los primeros 30 minutos son gratis y los siguientes 30 cuestan un dólar. A olvida la segunda media hora; C cobra también la parte gratuita.

screen.title: Accessibility Office: exam accommodations
text: Accessibility Services — Requesting Exam Accommodations

Students registered with Accessibility Services who need extended time or a separate room for an exam must submit a request through the online portal at least seven days before the exam. Requests submitted later will be considered only if space and staff are available, and approval cannot be guaranteed. Instructors are notified automatically once a request is approved, so students need not deliver letters in person. Accommodations approved for midterm exams do not carry over to final exams; a new request is required for each.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To explain how and when students should ask for special exam arrangements
To announce that the Accessibility Services office is moving to a new building
To tell instructors how to prepare separate rooms for their final exams
To invite students to register with Accessibility Services before midterms

why.en: Main purpose (paraphrase): the notice sets out the procedure and the deadline for accommodation requests. C reverses the audience: instructors are only notified. D is a precondition, not the purpose.
why.tr: Ana amaç (parafraz): duyuru düzenleme taleplerinin nasıl ve ne zamana kadar yapılacağını anlatıyor. C hitap edilen kişiyi tersine çeviriyor; öğretim üyeleri yalnızca bilgilendiriliyor. D bir ön koşul, amaç değil.
why.es: Propósito principal (paráfrasis): el aviso explica el procedimiento y el plazo para pedir adaptaciones. C invierte el destinatario: a los profesores solo se les avisa. D es un requisito previo, no el propósito.

questions.stem: A student submits a request four days before an exam. What can be inferred?
options: The request will be rejected without being reviewed
The student must deliver a letter to the instructor in person
The request might be approved, but only if resources allow
The exam will be moved to give the office more time

why.en: Inference: late requests are "considered only if space and staff are available", so approval is possible but uncertain. A goes too far ("rejected without being reviewed"); B contradicts "need not deliver letters in person".
why.tr: Çıkarım: geç talepler "yer ve personel varsa" değerlendiriliyor; onay mümkün ama kesin değil. A fazla ileri gidiyor ("incelenmeden reddedilir"); B "need not deliver letters in person" ifadesiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: las solicitudes tardías se consideran "solo si hay espacio y personal", así que la aprobación es posible pero no segura. A va demasiado lejos ("rechazada sin revisarla"); B contradice "need not deliver letters in person".

questions.stem: According to the notice, what must a student who had extended time for a midterm do before the final exam?
options: Nothing, because the midterm arrangement continues automatically
Ask the instructor to sign a letter confirming the arrangement
Register again with Accessibility Services as a new student
Ask once more, because each permission lasts for one exam period

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): approvals "do not carry over to final exams; a new request is required". A is the trap: it assumes the midterm approval continues. C confuses a new request with a new registration.
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): onaylar "final sınavlarına geçmiyor; yeni bir talep gerekiyor". A tuzak: ara sınav onayının sürdüğünü varsayıyor. C yeni talebi yeni kayıtla karıştırıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): las aprobaciones "no se trasladan a los exámenes finales; se necesita una nueva solicitud". A es la trampa: supone que la aprobación del parcial sigue. C confunde una nueva solicitud con un nuevo registro.

screen.title: Email: tuition payment plan
text:
From: Student Accounts Office
To: Daniel Okafor
Subject: Your payment plan request

Dear Daniel, thank you for applying to pay this semester's tuition in installments. Your plan has been approved: the balance will be divided into four equal payments, due on the first day of each month from September to December. There is a one-time setup fee of $25, which will be added to your first payment. Please note that a payment more than ten days late will cancel the plan, and the full remaining balance will then be due at once.
— Student Accounts Office

questions.stem: Why did the office write to Daniel?
options: To confirm that his request to pay in parts was accepted
To remind him that his first payment is already overdue
To explain why his application for a payment plan was refused
To ask him to choose how many payments he would like to make

why.en: Purpose (paraphrase): "Your plan has been approved." B is not stated: no payment is late yet. C reverses the decision; D is wrong because the office has already set four payments.
why.tr: Amaç (parafraz): "Your plan has been approved." B metinde yok, henüz geciken bir ödeme yok. C kararı tersine çeviriyor; D yanlış, çünkü ofis dört taksiti zaten belirlemiş.
why.es: Propósito (paráfrasis): "Your plan has been approved." B no se dice: todavía no hay ningún pago atrasado. C invierte la decisión; D es incorrecta porque la oficina ya fijó cuatro pagos.

questions.stem: What is true about the $25 fee?
options: It is charged every month together with each payment
It will be paid as part of the September payment
It is charged only if a payment arrives late
It can be avoided by paying the full balance in December

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): the fee is "one-time" and "added to your first payment", which is due in September. A contradicts "one-time"; C confuses the fee with the late-payment rule.
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): ücret "tek seferlik" ve "ilk ödemeye ekleniyor"; ilk ödeme Eylül'de. A "one-time" ifadesiyle çelişiyor; C ücreti gecikme kuralıyla karıştırıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): la tarifa es "one-time" y se "añade al primer pago", que vence en septiembre. A contradice "one-time"; C confunde la tarifa con la regla de los pagos atrasados.

questions.stem: What would happen if Daniel paid his October installment on October 15?
options: He would be charged a second setup fee of $25
His November payment would be moved to a later date
He would have to pay everything he still owes immediately
Nothing would happen, because payments may be up to twenty days late

why.en: Inference: October 15 is fourteen days late, more than ten, so the plan is cancelled and "the full remaining balance" becomes due. D invents a twenty-day limit; A and B are never mentioned.
why.tr: Çıkarım: 15 Ekim on dört gün gecikme demek, yani on günden fazla; plan iptal olur ve "kalan borcun tamamı" ödenmeli. D yirmi günlük bir süre uyduruyor; A ve B hiç geçmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: el 15 de octubre son catorce días de retraso, más de diez, así que el plan se cancela y vence "todo el saldo pendiente". D inventa un límite de veinte días; A y B no se mencionan.

screen.title: Library notice: booking study rooms
text: Group Study Rooms — Now Booked Through the Campus App

Starting Monday, the paper sign-up sheets outside the group study rooms will be removed. Rooms can be reserved up to three days ahead in the Campus app, for a maximum of two hours a day per student. If your group has not arrived within fifteen minutes of the start time, the room will be released to anyone waiting. Students without a smartphone can ask the staff at the circulation desk to book a room for them.

questions.stem: What is the notice mainly about?
options: A new procedure for getting a place to work with classmates
New opening hours for the library during exam weeks
A plan to add more group study rooms to the library
Rules about the noise level allowed in the group study rooms

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): rooms are now reserved in the app instead of on paper sheets. B, C and D bring in topics the notice never mentions (hours, new rooms, noise).
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): odalar artık kâğıt listeler yerine uygulamadan ayırtılıyor. B, C ve D duyuruda hiç geçmeyen konular getiriyor (saatler, yeni odalar, gürültü).
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): las salas ahora se reservan en la app en lugar de en hojas de papel. B, C y D introducen temas que el aviso no menciona (horarios, salas nuevas, ruido).

questions.stem: A group reserved a room for 3:00 but arrives at 3:20. What will most likely happen?
options: They will keep the room but lose twenty minutes of their time
They will have to ask the circulation desk to extend the booking
They may find that the room has been given to someone else
They will not be allowed to book a room again that week

why.en: Inference: a room is "released to anyone waiting" after fifteen minutes, so at 3:20 it may already be taken. A assumes the booking still stands; D invents a penalty the notice does not state.
why.tr: Çıkarım: on beş dakika içinde gelinmezse oda "bekleyen herkese" açılıyor; 3.20'de oda başkasına verilmiş olabilir. A rezervasyonun sürdüğünü varsayıyor; D duyuruda olmayan bir ceza uyduruyor.
why.es: Inferencia: la sala se "libera para quien esté esperando" a los quince minutos, así que a las 3:20 puede estar ocupada. A supone que la reserva sigue; D inventa una sanción que el aviso no menciona.

Can you describe a time when your usual way of getting to campus didn't work, and what you did instead?
Some people think universities should reduce the number of parking spaces to encourage students to take the bus or ride bicycles. What is your opinion?
How do you think the way students travel to campus will change over the next ten years, and why?

How do you think student clubs will change over the next ten years, especially as more activities move online?

screen.prompt: Your professor is teaching a class on higher education. Write a post responding to the professor's question. Express and support your opinion, and make a contribution to the discussion in your own words.

professor.name: Halvorsen
professor.post: Many universities now require students to complete an internship before they graduate. Supporters say internships teach practical skills that classes cannot. Others argue that a required internship is unfair to students who already work part-time or who cannot afford to accept an unpaid position. Should universities make an internship a graduation requirement? Why or why not?

students.name: Priya
students.post: I think they should. My cousin did an internship at an engineering firm, and she said she learned more about teamwork in three months than in two years of group projects. Employers also expect some experience now, so a requirement protects students from graduating without any.

students.name: Marcus
students.post: I disagree. I already work twenty hours a week to pay my rent, so an unpaid internship would mean losing my job. A requirement sounds fair, but it really helps students whose families can support them. Universities should encourage internships, not force them.

screen.prompt: Your professor is teaching a class on education. Write a post responding to the professor's question. Express and support your opinion, and make a contribution to the discussion in your own words.

professor.name: Okafor
professor.post: Many universities are debating whether every lecture should be recorded and posted online. Supporters say recordings help students review difficult material and help those who sometimes have to miss class because of work or family responsibilities. Others worry that if recordings are always available, fewer students will come to class, and discussions in the room will suffer. Should universities require professors to record all of their lectures? Why or why not?

students.name: Lucia
students.post: Yes, I think they should. Before my chemistry exam, I watched two lectures again, and parts I had missed the first time finally made sense. Also, many students have long commutes or part-time jobs. With a recording, missing one bus doesn't mean missing the material.

students.name: Tomas
students.post: I don't think it should be required. When my statistics professor started posting recordings, attendance dropped by almost half, and the few students who came rarely asked questions. Some professors also feel uncomfortable being recorded. Each professor should decide what works for their own course.

screen.prompt: Your professor is teaching a class on education policy. Write a post responding to the professor's question. Express and support your opinion, and make a contribution to the discussion in your own words.

professor.name: Lindqvist
professor.post: Laptops have become essential for almost every course. Some universities now give each new student a laptop and include the cost in tuition fees. Others keep fees lower and run a loan program instead, lending laptops for a few days or a whole semester to students who need one. Both approaches aim to make sure that no student falls behind. Which approach do you think serves students better, and why?

students.name: Amara
students.post: I think every student should receive a laptop. When only some students borrow one, everyone can see who could not afford their own, and that can be embarrassing. Also, if everyone has the same model, professors can plan assignments around the same software without worrying about whether it will run on each student's computer.

students.name: Tomás
students.post: I'd prefer a loan program. Most students already arrive with a laptop, so giving everyone another one wastes money and creates more electronic waste. A loan program keeps fees lower and still helps students whose computer breaks in the middle of the term, which is exactly when they need help the most.

professor.name: Okonkwo
professor.post: Many universities let students take a few courses outside their major on a pass/fail basis instead of receiving a letter grade. Supporters say this encourages students to explore subjects they would otherwise avoid. Critics worry that students put in less effort when a grade does not count. Should universities allow students to take some courses pass/fail? Why or why not?

students.name: Lena
students.post: Yes, they should. I wanted to take a physics course last year, but I was afraid a low grade would hurt my scholarship, so I chose something easier instead. With a pass/fail option, students can try difficult subjects without risking their grade average, and that is what university should be about.

students.name: Marco
students.post: I'm not convinced. When I know a grade does not really matter, I study only enough to pass, and I think many students are the same. Employers and graduate schools also look closely at transcripts, so a list of passes might make it harder to see what a student actually learned.

screen.prompt: Your professor is teaching a class on urban studies. Write a post responding to the professor's question. Express and support your opinion, and make a contribution to the discussion in your own words.

professor.name: Okafor
professor.post: Some cities have closed their historic centers to private cars, allowing only pedestrians, bicycles and public transport. Supporters say this makes city centers cleaner and more pleasant; critics argue that it hurts local businesses and makes life harder for residents. Should more cities ban private cars from their historic centers? Why or why not?

students.name: Lin
students.post: Yes. When my hometown closed its old town to cars, the streets became quieter and cafés put tables outside. More people came to walk around, so many shops actually did better than before.

students.name: Daniel
students.post: I disagree. Older people and people with disabilities often rely on cars, and buses don't reach every street. A total ban punishes the people who have the fewest alternatives.
